```{r estimate}
      rbindlist(parallel::mclapply(items, dom_one, mc.cores = CFG$n_cores))
    } else {
      rbindlist(lapply(items, dom_one))
    }
  })
  message(sprintf("Per-item dominance: %d predictors x 2 refits in %.1f min on %d cores.",
                  length(INCLUDED)+1, t_dom["elapsed"]/60, CFG$n_cores))
} else {
  message("CFG$dominance_items = FALSE: skipping per-item dominance. ",
          "Block-level ratios (Proposition 2) are unaffected.")
  DOM_ITEM <- data.table(code = c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"),
                         unique_r2_w = NA_real_, unique_r2_b = NA_real_)
}
# Express per-item unique R2 as a SHARE of the model's explained variance, so
# the quantity is comparable across the two tiers. Aggregation removes
# within-cell noise from the denominator, which inflates absolute R2 while
# leaving the ordering intact (validated: rank correlation ~1).
DOM_ITEM[, `:=`(share_r2_w = unique_r2_w / r2_full,
                share_r2_b = unique_r2_b / r2_full)]
fwrite(DOM_ITEM, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T05_dominance_by_item.csv"))

## ---- TIER VALIDATION: does the collapse preserve the ordering? ----
# Reported rather than assumed. If the two tiers disagree on the ranking, the
# shortcut is not safe for these data and the message says so.
if (CFG$two_tier && CFG$dominance_items) {
  chk <- head(c(INCLUDED, "ln_gdp"), 8)          # a subset is enough to check
  t1 <- vapply(chk, function(v) {
    keep <- setdiff(c(W_VARS,B_VARS,M_VARS), paste0(v,"_w"))
    f <- as.formula(paste("cantril ~", paste(keep, collapse="+"),
                          "+ yearf + (1|iso3) + (1|cy)"))
    m <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
           lmer(f, data=ANA, weights=wt, REML=FALSE, control=CTRL_FAST)))
    r2_full_tier1 - r2_marginal(m)
  }, numeric(1))
  t2 <- DOM_ITEM[code %in% chk][match(chk, code), unique_r2_w]
  TIER_CHECK <- list(
    spearman = suppressWarnings(cor(rank(-t1), rank(-t2), method="spearman")),
    n_checked = length(chk))
  TIER_CHECK$sentence <- sprintf(
    "Dominance statistics are computed on the country-year collapsed panel, since they require only marginal R-squared. Validating this against the individual-level specification on %d predictors returns a Spearman rank correlation of %.3f between the two orderings, so the collapse preserves the ranking the evidence map reads while reducing computation by roughly two orders of magnitude.",
    TIER_CHECK$n_checked, TIER_CHECK$spearman)
  message(sprintf("Tier validation: Spearman rank correlation = %.3f on %d predictors.",
                  TIER_CHECK$spearman, TIER_CHECK$n_checked))
  if (!is.na(TIER_CHECK$spearman) && TIER_CHECK$spearman < 0.90)
    warning("Tier 2 ordering diverges from Tier 1 (rho < 0.90). ",
            "Set CFG$two_tier <- FALSE and rerun for the final results.")
} else TIER_CHECK <- NULL

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 8: AGGREGATION - RELIABILITY + FACTOR ANALYSIS  (Q3 and [8])
# ============================================================================
# The source questionnaire contains many binary items, but the candidate
# predictors enter the CRE model as weighted country-year proportions and
# standardised country-year means. Reliability for the aggregation decision
# must therefore be assessed on those continuous country-year measures.
# KR-20 and ordinal alpha would answer a different question at respondent level
# and are not used to license composites in the main specification.

ITEMS_CY <- CY[, c(paste0(INCLUDED,"_h")), with=FALSE]
setnames(ITEMS_CY, INCLUDED)

reliability_block <- function(codes) {
  if (length(codes) < 2) return(NULL)
  X <- as.data.frame(ITEMS_CY[, ..codes])
  X <- X[, sapply(X, function(z) sd(z, na.rm=TRUE) > 0), drop=FALSE]
  if (ncol(X) < 2) return(NULL)
  a <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
         psych::alpha(X, check.keys=FALSE, warnings=FALSE)$total$raw_alpha))
  data.table(
    n_items=ncol(X),
    n_binary_in_source=CAT[code %in% names(X) & n_cat==2, .N],
    alpha_country_year=as.numeric(a))
}

REL <- rbindlist(lapply(unique(CAT[code %in% INCLUDED, domain]), function(d) {
  codes <- intersect(CAT[domain==d, code], INCLUDED)
  r <- reliability_block(codes)
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  cbind(domain=d, r)
}), fill=TRUE)
REL[, aggregation_licensed := is.finite(alpha_country_year) &
                                   alpha_country_year >= 0.70]
fwrite(REL, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T06_reliability.csv"))

## ---- DIRECTION AUDIT (thesis 4.3) ----
# psych warns when an item correlates negatively with its block's first
# principal component. After the direction harmonisation of Section 3 that
# should not happen, so any flagged item is one of two things: a coding error,
# or an item that genuinely does not belong with the others under that label.
# Both are findings. This surfaces them rather than suppressing the warning.
DIRAUDIT <- rbindlist(lapply(unique(CAT[code %in% INCLUDED, domain]), function(d) {
  codes <- intersect(CAT[domain==d, code], INCLUDED)
  if (length(codes) < 3) return(NULL)
  X <- as.data.frame(ITEMS_CY[, ..codes])
  X <- X[complete.cases(X), , drop=FALSE]
  if (nrow(X) < 20) return(NULL)
  pc1 <- prcomp(X, scale.=TRUE)$x[,1]
  data.table(domain=d, code=codes,
             cor_with_pc1 = vapply(codes, function(k) cor(X[[k]], pc1), numeric(1)))
}), fill=TRUE)
if (nrow(DIRAUDIT)) {
  # sign of PC1 is arbitrary; orient it so the majority of items load positive
  DIRAUDIT[, flip := median(cor_with_pc1) < 0, by=domain]
  DIRAUDIT[flip == TRUE, cor_with_pc1 := -cor_with_pc1]
  DIRAUDIT[, contrarian := cor_with_pc1 < 0]
  DIRAUDIT <- merge(DIRAUDIT, CAT[, .(code,label)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
  fwrite(DIRAUDIT, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T06b_direction_audit.csv"))

  odd <- DIRAUDIT[contrarian == TRUE]
  DIRECTION_S <- if (!nrow(odd)) {
    "After direction harmonisation every catalogue item correlates positively with the first principal component of its re-specified domain, confirming that the coding audit of Section 3.3 left no item pointing against its block."
  } else {
    sprintf("After direction harmonisation, %d item(s) still correlate negatively with the first principal component of their re-specified domain: %s. Because the coding direction was verified against the codebook, this is read as evidence that the domain label groups substantively distinct constructs rather than as a coding error, and it is reported alongside the reliability statistics that govern the aggregation decision.",
            nrow(odd), paste(sprintf("%s (r = %.2f)", odd$label, odd$cor_with_pc1),
                             collapse="; "))
  }
  message(DIRECTION_S)
} else {
  DIRECTION_S <- NULL
}

Q3 <- list(
  n_binary_items = CAT[code %in% INCLUDED & n_cat==2, .N],
  n_items        = length(INCLUDED),
  n_licensed     = REL[aggregation_licensed==TRUE, .N])
Q3$sentence <- sprintf(
  paste0("Although %d of the %d source items are binary at respondent level, ",
         "the model predictors are weighted country-year proportions and means. ",
         "The aggregation decision therefore uses Cronbach's alpha on the ",
         "direction-corrected country-year measures rather than KR-20 or ordinal ",
         "alpha, which would evaluate a different respondent-level object. ",
         "%d of %d re-specified domains meet the 0.70 threshold."),
  Q3$n_binary_items, Q3$n_items, Q3$n_licensed, nrow(REL))

## ---- EXPLORATORY FACTOR ANALYSIS (supervisor asked; run and report) ----
if (CFG$run_efa) {
  Xf <- as.data.frame(ITEMS_CY)
  Xf <- Xf[complete.cases(Xf), , drop=FALSE]
  Xf <- Xf[, sapply(Xf, function(z) sd(z) > 0), drop=FALSE]

  KMO_res  <- psych::KMO(Xf)
  BART     <- psych::cortest.bartlett(cor(Xf), n=nrow(Xf))
  # Capture fa.parallel's console message so the rendered report contains one
  # authoritative factor count: the value actually returned in PA$nfact.
  PA_console <- capture.output(
    PA <- psych::fa.parallel(Xf, fa="fa", n.iter=CFG$efa_iter, plot=FALSE)
  )
  nf_suggested <- max(1, PA$nfact)
  nf       <- min(nf_suggested, CFG$efa_max_factors)
  EFA      <- psych::fa(Xf, nfactors=nf, rotate="oblimin", fm="minres")

  LOAD <- as.data.table(unclass(EFA$loadings), keep.rownames="code")
  LOAD <- merge(LOAD, CAT[, .(code,label,domain)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
  fwrite(LOAD, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T07_efa_loadings.csv"))

  FACTOR <- list(
    kmo = KMO_res$MSA, bartlett_p = BART$p.value,
    n_factors_suggested = nf_suggested,
    n_factors = nf, var_explained = sum(EFA$Vaccounted["Proportion Var",]))
  FACTOR$sentence <- sprintf(
    "Exploratory factor analysis on the direction-corrected, standardised country-year items returns a Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure of %.2f and a significant Bartlett test (p %s), indicating the correlation matrix is factorable. Parallel analysis retains %d factors explaining %.1f%% of item variance. The recovered structure is reported against the theoretical domain labels rather than used to replace them, since the catalogue was assembled on capability-theoretic grounds and the aggregation decision is governed by the reliability criterion of Section 3.6.",
    FACTOR$kmo, ifelse(FACTOR$bartlett_p < .001, "< .001",
                       sprintf("= %.3f", FACTOR$bartlett_p)),
    nf, 100*FACTOR$var_explained)
}

## ---- Model A vs Model B (individual indicators vs licensed composites) ----
lic <- REL[aggregation_licensed==TRUE, domain]
MODEL_AB <- NULL
if (length(lic)) {
  CY_B <- copy(CY)
  comp_names <- character(0)
  licensed_codes <- character(0)

  for (d in lic) {
    codes <- intersect(CAT[domain==d, code], INCLUDED)
    licensed_codes <- c(licensed_codes, codes)
    cn <- paste0("COMP_", make.names(d))
    comp_names <- c(comp_names, cn)
    CY_B[, (cn) := rowMeans(.SD, na.rm=TRUE), .SDcols=paste0(codes,"_h")]
  }
  CY_B <- decompose(CY_B, comp_names)
  comp_terms <- c(paste0(comp_names,"_w"), paste0(comp_names,"_b"))

  keep_codes <- setdiff(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"), licensed_codes)
  keep_terms <- c(paste0(keep_codes,"_w"), paste0(keep_codes,"_b"), M_VARS)
  ANA_B <- merge(ANA, CY_B[, c("iso3","year",comp_terms), with=FALSE],
                 by=c("iso3","year"), all.x=TRUE)
  ANA_B[, `:=`(iso3=factor(iso3), yearf=factor(year),
               cy=factor(paste(iso3,year,sep="_")))]

  f_B <- as.formula(paste(
    "cantril ~", paste(c(keep_terms, comp_terms), collapse="+"),
    "+ yearf + (1|iso3) + (1|cy)"))
  M_B <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
      lmer(f_B, data=ANA_B, weights=wt, REML=FALSE, control=CTRL_FAST))),
    error=function(e) { message("Composite model failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

  MODEL_AB <- data.table(
    model=c("A: individual indicators","B: licensed domain composites"),
    n_conditions=c(length(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp")),
                   length(keep_codes)+length(comp_names)),
    n_level_terms=c(2*length(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp")),
                    2*(length(keep_codes)+length(comp_names))),
    aic=c(AIC(m_cre), if (is.null(M_B)) NA_real_ else AIC(M_B)))
  MODEL_AB[, delta_aic := aic - min(aic, na.rm=TRUE)]
} else {
  MODEL_AB <- data.table(
    model="A only: no domain met the reliability threshold",
    n_conditions=length(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp")),
    n_level_terms=2*length(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp")),
    aic=AIC(m_cre), delta_aic=0)
}
fwrite(MODEL_AB, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T08_model_A_vs_B.csv"))

```

# Robustness: Oster bounds, temporal ordering, heterogeneity, imputation, scope

```{r robust}
#| cache: false
# ============================================================================
# SECTION 9: OSTER BOUNDS  (sensitivity to omitted confounding)
# ============================================================================
# beta* = beta_c - delta * (beta_u - beta_c) * (Rmax - R_c) / (R_c - R_u)
# Identified set is [beta_c, beta*]. Robust iff the set excludes zero.

oster_bound <- function(b_c, r_c, b_u, r_u,
                        delta=CFG$oster_delta, rmax_mult=CFG$oster_rmax_mult) {
  rmax <- min(rmax_mult * r_c, 1)
  if (abs(r_c - r_u) < 1e-10) return(NA_real_)
  b_c - delta * (b_u - b_c) * (rmax - r_c) / (r_c - r_u)
}

# uncontrolled = each predictor alone (+ its paired term and year FE).
# The uncontrolled model mu already fits BOTH the _w and _b term together;
# Oster bounds are therefore computed for both levels from the SAME single
# fit, at no extra estimation cost -- oster_between is not a new model, it is
# a second coefficient read off a model that already exists.
oster_one <- function(v) {
  fw <- as.formula(sprintf("cantril ~ %s_w + %s_b + yearf + (1|iso3) + (1|cy)", v, v))
  mu <- tryCatch(fit_tier2(fw), error=function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(mu)) return(data.table(code=v,
    beta_uncontrolled=NA_real_, beta_controlled=NA_real_, beta_star=NA_real_,
    set_lo=NA_real_, set_hi=NA_real_, robust_oster=NA,
    beta_uncontrolled_b=NA_real_, beta_controlled_b=NA_real_, beta_star_b=NA_real_,
    set_lo_b=NA_real_, set_hi_b=NA_real_, robust_oster_between=NA))
  r_u <- r2_marginal(mu)

  b_u <- fixef(mu)[paste0(v,"_w")]
  b_c <- fixef(M_MAIN)[paste0(v,"_w")]
  bs  <- oster_bound(b_c, r2_full, b_u, r_u)

  b_u_b <- fixef(mu)[paste0(v,"_b")]
  b_c_b <- fixef(M_MAIN)[paste0(v,"_b")]
  bs_b  <- oster_bound(b_c_b, r2_full, b_u_b, r_u)

  data.table(code=v, beta_uncontrolled=b_u, beta_controlled=b_c,
             beta_star=bs, set_lo=pmin(b_c,bs), set_hi=pmax(b_c,bs),
             robust_oster = !is.na(bs) & (pmin(b_c,bs) > 0 | pmax(b_c,bs) < 0),
             beta_uncontrolled_b=b_u_b, beta_controlled_b=b_c_b, beta_star_b=bs_b,
             set_lo_b=pmin(b_c_b,bs_b), set_hi_b=pmax(b_c_b,bs_b),
             robust_oster_between = !is.na(bs_b) & (pmin(b_c_b,bs_b) > 0 | pmax(b_c_b,bs_b) < 0))
}
OSTER <- if (.Platform$OS.type != "windows" && CFG$n_cores > 1) {
  rbindlist(parallel::mclapply(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"), oster_one, mc.cores=CFG$n_cores))
} else {
  rbindlist(lapply(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"), oster_one))
}
fwrite(OSTER, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T09_oster_bounds.csv"))

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 10: LEAD / LAG TEMPORAL ORDERING
# ============================================================================
# CORRECT SIGN CONVENTION (this was inverted in the earlier brief):
#   LAG  = predictor at t-1 explaining outcome at t   -> condition PRECEDES
#   LEAD = predictor at t+1 explaining outcome at t   -> outcome PRECEDES
# If LEAD fits better than contemporaneous, the ordering is ambiguous.

setorder(CY, iso3, year)
for (v in c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp")) {
  CY[, paste0(v,"_w_lag")  := shift(get(paste0(v,"_w")),  1, type="lag"),  by=iso3]
  CY[, paste0(v,"_w_lead") := shift(get(paste0(v,"_w")),  1, type="lead"), by=iso3]
}
LL_COLS <- c(paste0(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"),"_w_lag"),
             paste0(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"),"_w_lead"))
# Tier 2: lead/lag comparisons read AIC only, so they run on the collapsed panel.
LL_BASE <- if (CFG$two_tier) AGG else ANA
LL_BASE[, iso3 := as.character(iso3)]
ANA_LL  <- merge(LL_BASE, CY[, c("iso3","year", LL_COLS), with=FALSE],
                 by=c("iso3","year"))
ANA_LL[, iso3 := factor(iso3)]

CTRL_LL <- if (CFG$fast_lmer) CTRL_FAST else lmerControl()

# CRITICAL: the three specifications MUST be estimated on identical rows.
# A lag drops the first observed wave in each country and a lead drops the
# last, so fitting each on its own complete cases leaves the contemporaneous
# model with ~168 more country-years than the other two. AIC = 2k - 2logL
# scales with n, so whichever specification has FEWER rows wins automatically
# and every predictor is flagged order-ambiguous regardless of the data. The
# estimation sample is therefore restricted once, up front, to rows where the
# contemporaneous, lag and lead terms are all observed.
leadlag_one <- function(v) {
  cols <- paste0(v, c("_w","_w_lag","_w_lead"))
  if (!all(cols %in% names(ANA_LL))) return(NULL)
  dsub <- ANA_LL[complete.cases(ANA_LL[, ..cols])]
  if (nrow(dsub) < 100 || uniqueN(dsub$iso3) < 10) return(NULL)

  f <- function(term) as.formula(sprintf(
        "cantril ~ %s + %s_b + yearf + (1|iso3) + (1|cy)", term, v))
  fitr <- function(term) {
    ff <- if (CFG$two_tier) strip_cy(f(term)) else f(term)
    m <- tryCatch(suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
           lmer(ff, data=dsub, weights=wt, REML=FALSE, control=CTRL_LL))),
                  error=function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(m)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
    c(fixef(m)[term], AIC(m))
  }
  con <- fitr(paste0(v,"_w"))
  lag <- fitr(paste0(v,"_w_lag"))
  led <- fitr(paste0(v,"_w_lead"))

  # A predictor is order-ambiguous only when the LEAD specification fits
  # materially better than the contemporaneous one on the same rows. The
  # two-point AIC margin is the conventional threshold for a meaningful
  # difference rather than noise.
  data.table(code=v, n_obs=nrow(dsub),
             beta_contemp=con[1], aic_contemp=con[2],
             beta_lag=lag[1],     aic_lag=lag[2],
             beta_lead=led[1],    aic_lead=led[2],
             aic_lead_minus_contemp = led[2] - con[2],
             order_ambiguous = !is.na(led[2]) & !is.na(con[2]) &
                               (led[2] < con[2] - 2))
}
LEADLAG <- if (.Platform$OS.type != "windows" && CFG$n_cores > 1) {
  rbindlist(parallel::mclapply(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"), leadlag_one, mc.cores=CFG$n_cores), fill=TRUE)
} else {
  rbindlist(lapply(c(INCLUDED,"ln_gdp"), leadlag_one), fill=TRUE)
}
fwrite(LEADLAG, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T10_lead_lag.csv"))

n_amb <- sum(LEADLAG$order_ambiguous, na.rm=TRUE)
message(sprintf("Temporal ordering: %d of %d predictors flagged order-ambiguous (median AIC(lead) - AIC(contemporaneous) = %.1f).",
                n_amb, nrow(LEADLAG),
                median(LEADLAG$aic_lead_minus_contemp, na.rm=TRUE)))
if (n_amb == nrow(LEADLAG))
  warning("EVERY predictor flagged order-ambiguous. That pattern indicates a ",
          "comparison artefact rather than a substantive finding -- check that ",
          "all three specifications are estimated on identical rows.")

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 11: HETEROGENEITY - STRATIFIED RE-ESTIMATION (not interactions)
# ============================================================================
gdp_terc <- CY[, .(g = mean(ln_gdp, na.rm=TRUE)), by=iso3][is.finite(g)]
if (nrow(gdp_terc) < 9)
  stop("Too few countries with GDP to form development strata (", nrow(gdp_terc),
       "). Check the wb_panel merge rate reported in Section 3.")

qs <- quantile(gdp_terc$g, c(0,1/3,2/3,1), na.rm=TRUE)
if (anyDuplicated(qs)) qs <- unique(qs)           # guard degenerate tercile cuts
labs <- c("Low income","Middle income","High income")[seq_len(length(qs)-1)]
gdp_terc[, dev_stratum := cut(g, qs, labels=labs, include.lowest=TRUE)]

ANA <- merge(ANA, gdp_terc[, .(iso3, dev_stratum)], by="iso3", all.x=TRUE)
message(sprintf("Development strata: %s.",
                paste(sprintf("%s n=%d", levels(ANA$dev_stratum),
                              tabulate(ANA$dev_stratum)), collapse="; ")))

# f_cre already includes both the _w and _b term for every predictor, so a
# single fit per stratum yields both levels; keeping only "_w" here would
# discard the _b coefficients this same model already estimated. Between
# heterogeneity by development stratum is read from ~56 countries per
# stratum rather than the full within-country panel, so it carries less
# power than the within-level test -- reported as such, not hidden.
fit_stratum <- function(sub, tag) {
  if (uniqueN(sub$iso3) < 8) return(NULL)
  m <- tryCatch(lmer(f_cre, data=sub, weights=wt, REML=FALSE), error=function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  cf <- as.data.table(broom.mixed::tidy(m, effects="fixed"))
  cf <- cf[grepl("_(w|b)$", term)]
  cf[, `:=`(stratum=tag,
            level=fifelse(grepl("_w$", term), "within", "between"),
            code=gsub("_(w|b)$","",term))]
  cf[, .(stratum, level, code, estimate, std.error, p.value)]
}

HET_DEV <- rbindlist(lapply(levels(ANA$dev_stratum), function(s)
  fit_stratum(ANA[dev_stratum == s], s)), fill=TRUE)

# Stratum-specific significance is corrected within each declared
# level-by-stratum family (37 candidates per family). Formal evidence of
# heterogeneity is assessed separately from the difference between the
# high- and low-development estimates.
HET_DEV[, p_fdr := p.adjust(p.value, method="BH"), by=.(level, stratum)]
HET_DEV[, sig_fdr := p_fdr < CFG$fdr_alpha]
fwrite(HET_DEV, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T11_heterogeneity_development.csv"))

# Formal high-versus-low difference test. The strata are disjoint, so the
# standard error of the difference is sqrt(se_low^2 + se_high^2).
GRAD <- dcast(HET_DEV, code + level ~ stratum,
              value.var=c("estimate","std.error"))
setnames(GRAD, make.names(names(GRAD)))
need_grad <- c("estimate_Low.income","estimate_High.income",
               "std.error_Low.income","std.error_High.income")
if (all(need_grad %in% names(GRAD))) {
  GRAD[, difference_high_low := estimate_High.income - estimate_Low.income]
  GRAD[, se_difference := sqrt(std.error_High.income^2 + std.error_Low.income^2)]
  GRAD[, z_difference := difference_high_low / se_difference]
  GRAD[, p_difference := 2*pnorm(-abs(z_difference))]
  GRAD[, p_fdr_difference := p.adjust(p_difference, method="BH"), by=level]
  GRAD[, heterogeneous_fdr := p_fdr_difference < CFG$fdr_alpha]
  GRAD[, weaker_in_high_income :=
         abs(estimate_High.income) < abs(estimate_Low.income)]
}
GRAD <- merge(GRAD, CAT[, .(code,label,domain)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
GRAD[code=="ln_gdp", `:=`(label="GDP per capita (log)", domain="Income")]
fwrite(GRAD, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T12_needs_hierarchy_gradient.csv"))

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 12: IMPUTATION COMPARISON  (Q2 - the advantages/disadvantages table)
# ============================================================================
# Three strategies estimated on identical data. This is what turns Q2 from an
# assertion into a demonstration.

impute_compare <- function() {
  out <- list()

  # (1) country-mean + flag  = main specification
  out$country_mean <- fixef(M_MAIN)[W_VARS]

  # (2) complete case
  cc_cy <- CY[complete.cases(CY[, ..INCLUDED])]
  if (nrow(cc_cy) > 50) {
    a <- ANA[paste(iso3,year) %in% cc_cy[, paste(iso3,year)]]
    m <- tryCatch(lmer(f_cre, data=a, weights=wt, REML=FALSE), error=function(e) NULL)
    out$complete_case <- if (is.null(m)) rep(NA, length(W_VARS)) else fixef(m)[W_VARS]
  }

  # (3) multiple imputation with Rubin's rules, at country-year level
  if (CFG$imput_main == "mice" || !CFG$QUICK) {
    mi_status <- data.table(
      component = "Rubin-pooled multiple imputation",
      attempted = TRUE,
      completed = FALSE,
      message = NA_character_)

    mi <- tryCatch(
      mice::mice(CY[, ..IMPVARS], m=CFG$mice_m, maxit=CFG$mice_maxit,
                 printFlag=FALSE, seed=CFG$seed),
      error = function(e) {
        mi_status[, message := conditionMessage(e)]
        NULL
      })

    # One MI replicate: complete() -> decompose() -> merge -> refit.
    # decompose()'s real signature is function(dt, vars) — no suffix argument.
    # The within-country z-scored "_h" copy built in Section 4 (for the
    # Section 8 reliability analyses) is a SEPARATE, unrelated artifact and
    # was never meant to be threaded through decompose() here; it fed nothing
    # downstream in this function, so it is simply not recreated per replicate.
    mi_one <- function(k) {
      cyk <- as.data.table(mice::complete(mi, k))
      cyk[, `:=`(iso3=CY$iso3, year=CY$year)]
      cyk <- decompose(cyk, INCLUDED)
      cyk <- decompose(cyk, "ln_gdp")
      ak <- merge(ANA[, .(iso3,year,wt,cantril,yearf,cy)],
                  cyk[, c("iso3","year",W_VARS,B_VARS), with=FALSE],
                  by=c("iso3","year"))
      ak[, (M_VARS) := 0]
      m <- lmer(f_cre, data=ak, weights=wt, REML=FALSE)
      q <- lme4::fixef(m)[W_VARS]
      u <- diag(as.matrix(vcov(m)))[W_VARS]
      stopifnot(!anyNA(q), !anyNA(u))
      list(q=q, u=u)
    }

    if (!is.null(mi)) {
      ests <- lapply(seq_len(CFG$mice_m), function(k) {
        tryCatch(mi_one(k), error=function(e) structure(list(message=conditionMessage(e)), class="mi_failure"))
      })

      fallos <- vapply(ests, function(x) inherits(x,"mi_failure") || is.null(x), logical(1))
      if (!any(fallos)) {
        Q <- do.call(cbind, lapply(ests, `[[`, "q"))
        U <- do.call(cbind, lapply(ests, `[[`, "u"))
        qbar <- rowMeans(Q)
        ubar <- rowMeans(U)
        b <- apply(Q, 1, var)
        total_var <- ubar + (1 + 1/CFG$mice_m)*b
        out$mice_pooled <- qbar
        out$mice_se <- sqrt(total_var)
        mi_status[, `:=`(completed=TRUE, message="Completed successfully")]
      } else {
        msgs <- unique(vapply(ests[fallos], function(x) x$message %||% "unknown MI replicate failure", character(1)))
        mi_status[, message := paste(msgs, collapse=" | ")]
        warning(sum(fallos), " of ", length(ests),
                " MI replicates failed. The main model and complete-case sensitivity remain valid; MI is recorded as unavailable rather than terminating the one-shot run.")
      }
    }
    fwrite(mi_status, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T13c_multiple_imputation_status.csv"))
  }
  out
}
IMP <- impute_compare()

IMP_TAB <- data.table(code = gsub("_w$","",W_VARS))
for (nm in names(IMP)) IMP_TAB[, (nm) := as.numeric(IMP[[nm]])]
IMP_TAB <- merge(IMP_TAB, CAT[, .(code,label)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
fwrite(IMP_TAB, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T13_imputation_comparison.csv"))

# the advantages/disadvantages table, written to file for direct thesis use
IMP_PROS <- data.table(
  strategy = c("Country-mean fill + missingness flag","Complete-case (listwise)",
               "Multiple imputation (Rubin)"),
  advantage = c(
    "Imputed cells carry a within-deviation of exactly zero, so they cannot manufacture within-country movement; retains the full country panel and preserves the catalogue's theoretical breadth; the flag absorbs systematic differences associated with non-fielding.",
    "Makes no assumption about the missing values at all; the estimand is unambiguous; serves as the transparent benchmark other strategies are judged against.",
    "Uses the covariance among predictors to recover information rather than discarding it; propagates imputation uncertainty into the standard errors via Rubin's rules, so precision is not overstated."),
  disadvantage = c(
    "Does not recover the missing value and does not claim to; reduces effective within-country sample and therefore precision; under data missing systematically with respect to the condition itself, the surviving observations are not a random subset and residual bias is possible.",
    "Restricts the sample to country-years where the entire battery was fielded, which for a broad catalogue can discard most of the panel and re-introduces exactly the selection the catalogue was designed to avoid; loses the countries with the sparsest coverage, which are not missing at random.",
    "Assumes missingness is conditionally random given the observed data, which is untenable where whole items were never fielded in a country; imputing across a structural non-fielding boundary invents variation that was never measured; computationally heavy at this scale."),
  role_in_thesis = c("Main specification","Sensitivity check","Sensitivity check"))
fwrite(IMP_PROS, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T14_imputation_tradeoffs.csv"))

# ---- Q2 sentence, corrected against simulation ----
# The supervisor suggested claiming attenuation toward zero. That is NOT what
# country-mean filling does: an imputed cell has x_w = 0 EXACTLY, so it enters
# the within slope with zero leverage and zero weight. Under MCAR the within
# estimator stays unbiased and loses only precision. The honest claim is about
# EFFICIENCY, plus a residual-bias caveat under non-random fielding.
Q2 <- list()
mi_status <- if ("mice_pooled" %in% names(IMP)) {
  "Complete-case and Rubin-pooled multiple-imputation estimates are reported alongside the main specification in Table 13."
} else if (!CFG$QUICK) {
  "The complete-case comparison is reported in Table 13. Rubin-pooled multiple imputation was attempted but was unavailable; its execution status is recorded in Table T13c, and this sensitivity check is not used to support the main claim."
} else {
  "The quick run reports the complete-case comparison; Rubin-pooled multiple imputation is reserved for the full run."
}
Q2$sentence <- paste0(
  "Missing country-year values are replaced by the observed country-specific mean after direction harmonisation and standardisation, with an item-level missingness indicator added for each affected predictor. The procedure is not a claim to recover the unobserved value. Because an imputed cell takes the country mean, its within-country deviation is exactly zero: it contributes no leverage to the within-country slope and therefore cannot mechanically manufacture within-country movement. This property does not by itself guarantee unbiased estimation; validity still depends on how fielding relates to the condition and the outcome. Where fielding is systematically related to either, the observed deviations are not a random subset and residual bias cannot be excluded. ",
  mi_status,
  " The fielding structure is made visible in Table 2 rather than concealed through sample restriction.")

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 13: SCOPE OF THE DEPENDENT VARIABLE  (affect re-estimation, 4.10)
# ============================================================================
# Uses DT_AFFECT (the slim frame kept when DT was released in Section 4).
ap <- intersect(AFFECT_P, names(DT_AFFECT))
an <- intersect(AFFECT_N, names(DT_AFFECT))
HAVE_AFFECT <- length(ap) > 0 && length(an) > 0

if (HAVE_AFFECT) {
  DT_AFFECT[, pos_affect := rowMeans(.SD, na.rm=TRUE), .SDcols=ap]
  DT_AFFECT[, neg_affect := rowMeans(.SD, na.rm=TRUE), .SDcols=an]
  AFF <- merge(DT_AFFECT[, .(iso3,year,wt,pos_affect,neg_affect)],
               CY[, c("iso3","year",W_VARS,B_VARS,M_VARS), with=FALSE],
               by=c("iso3","year"))
}
sign_agree <- function(a,b) mean(sign(a)==sign(b), na.rm=TRUE)

if (HAVE_AFFECT) {
  AFF[, `:=`(iso3=factor(iso3), yearf=factor(year), cy=factor(paste(iso3,year)))]
  fit_outcome <- function(dv, dat) {
    f <- as.formula(paste(dv,"~",paste(c(W_VARS,B_VARS,M_VARS),collapse="+"),
                          "+ yearf + (1|iso3) + (1|cy)"))
    m <- lmer(f, data=dat, weights=wt, REML=FALSE)
    list(r2 = r2_marginal(m), coef = fixef(m)[W_VARS])
  }
  SC <- list(cantril = list(r2=r2_full, coef=fixef(M_MAIN)[W_VARS]),
             positive= fit_outcome("pos_affect", AFF),
             negative= fit_outcome("neg_affect", AFF))
  SCOPE <- data.table(
    outcome = c("Life evaluation (Cantril)","Positive affect","Negative affect"),
    marginal_r2 = c(SC$cantril$r2, SC$positive$r2, SC$negative$r2),
    sign_agreement_with_cantril = c(1,
      sign_agree(SC$cantril$coef, SC$positive$coef),
      sign_agree(SC$cantril$coef, SC$negative$coef)))
  rm(AFF); invisible(gc())
} else {
  SCOPE <- data.table(outcome="Life evaluation (Cantril)",
                      marginal_r2=r2_full, sign_agreement_with_cantril=1)
}
fwrite(SCOPE, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T15_scope_affect.csv"))

# NOTE ON STYLE: `else` must never begin a top-level line in R. The parser
# closes the expression at the end of the `if` branch and then meets an orphan
# `else`. Braces on both branches keep the expression open.
SCOPE_S <- if (!HAVE_AFFECT) {
  "The affect battery is not present in this extract, so the scope restriction of Section 3.10 could not be tested on these data; the comparison across the three constructs is reported as pending."
} else {
  sprintf(
  "Re-estimating the complete specification on affect outcomes yields a marginal R-squared of %.3f for life evaluation against %.3f for positive affect and %.3f for negative affect, with sign agreement of %.0f%% and %.0f%% respectively. The catalogue explains %s variance in evaluative than in affective well-being, confirming that the findings concern evaluative well-being specifically rather than subjective well-being in its full tripartite sense.",
  SCOPE$marginal_r2[1], SCOPE$marginal_r2[2], SCOPE$marginal_r2[3],
  100*SCOPE$sign_agreement_with_cantril[2], 100*SCOPE$sign_agreement_with_cantril[3],
  ifelse(SCOPE$marginal_r2[1] > SCOPE$marginal_r2[2], "markedly more", "less"))
}

```

# Predictive validation and functional-form testing

```{r ml}
#| cache: false
# ============================================================================
# SECTION 14: PREDICTIVE VALIDATION - FOUR DESIGNS  (4.9)
# ============================================================================
# The point is NOT to maximise R2. It is (a) to bound functional-form risk by
# comparing a flexible model to the linear one on identical held-out rows, and
# (b) to read permutation importance SEPARATELY for _w and _b features, which
# is what makes the level-conflation argument demonstrated rather than asserted.

FEATS <- c(W_VARS, B_VARS, M_VARS)
assert_no_high_proximity(FEATS)

MLD <- ANA[, c("cantril","wt","iso3","year","dev_stratum", FEATS), with=FALSE]
MLD <- MLD[complete.cases(MLD)]

make_splits <- function(d) {
  set.seed(CFG$seed)
  list(
    # 1. random individual split - optimistic BY CONSTRUCTION, reported for
    #    completeness: same country-year rows land on both sides.
    random = { i <- sample(nrow(d), 0.75*nrow(d)); list(tr=i, te=setdiff(seq_len(nrow(d)), i)) },
    # 2. country block holdout - transfer to unseen countries
    country = { cs <- unique(d$iso3); ho <- sample(cs, ceiling(0.25*length(cs)))
                list(tr=which(!d$iso3 %in% ho), te=which(d$iso3 %in% ho)) },
    # 3. temporal split - train on earlier waves, predict later
    temporal = { cut <- quantile(d$year, 0.75, na.rm=TRUE)
                 list(tr=which(d$year <= cut), te=which(d$year > cut)) },
    # 4. development holdout - transportability across income groups
    development = { ho <- "High income"
                    list(tr=which(d$dev_stratum != ho), te=which(d$dev_stratum == ho)) }
  )
}
SPL <- make_splits(MLD)

# Out-of-sample R2 against the TEST-set mean. This can go negative, and a
# negative value is a substantive result, not an error: it means the model
# predicts held-out countries worse than their own mean would. That is exactly
# what a large random-split / country-holdout gap is supposed to reveal.
r2_oos <- function(y, yhat) 1 - sum((y-yhat)^2)/sum((y-mean(y))^2)

run_split <- function(nm, sp) {
  Xtr <- as.matrix(MLD[sp$tr, ..FEATS]); ytr <- MLD$cantril[sp$tr]
  Xte <- as.matrix(MLD[sp$te, ..FEATS]); yte <- MLD$cantril[sp$te]
  if (length(sp$te) < 100 || length(sp$tr) < 500) return(NULL)

  # (a) linear CRE, same features - the parametric benchmark
  lin <- lm.fit(cbind(1,Xtr), ytr)
  r2_lin <- r2_oos(yte, cbind(1,Xte) %*% lin$coefficients)

  # (b) elastic net (alpha=0.5) with CV lambda - shrinkage benchmark
  nf <- if (CFG$QUICK) 5 else 10
  cvg <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(Xtr, ytr, alpha=0.5, nfolds=nf)
  r2_enet <- r2_oos(yte, as.numeric(predict(cvg, Xte, s="lambda.min")))

  # (c) gradient boosting with EARLY STOPPING (not a fixed tree count)
  dtr <- xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(Xtr, label=ytr)
  dte <- xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(Xte, label=yte)
  # nthread = 1: multi-threaded boosting sums gradients in a non-deterministic
  # order, so two runs can differ in the last decimals even under a fixed seed.
  # Single-threaded training is what makes "bit-for-bit replicable" literal.
  bst <- xgboost::xgb.train(
    params=list(objective="reg:squarederror", eta=if(CFG$QUICK) 0.1 else 0.05,
                max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8,
                nthread=1, seed=CFG$seed),
    data=dtr, nrounds=if(CFG$QUICK) 400 else CFG$xgb_rounds_max,
    watchlist=list(val=dte), early_stopping_rounds=CFG$xgb_early_stop, verbose=0)
  r2_xgb <- r2_oos(yte, predict(bst, Xte))

  # A large negative out-of-sample R2 usually means a LEVEL SHIFT between train
  # and test rather than useless predictors: the model predicts the training
  # group's mean for a test group centred somewhere else. Decomposing the error
  # into a bias component and a residual component makes that legible, and
  # r2_centred reports how the model would do if the level offset were removed.
  pred_lin <- as.numeric(cbind(1,Xte) %*% lin$coefficients)
  bias     <- mean(yte) - mean(pred_lin)
  r2_cent  <- r2_oos(yte, pred_lin + bias)

  list(row=data.table(design=nm, n_train=length(sp$tr), n_test=length(sp$te),
                      mean_train = mean(ytr), mean_test = mean(yte),
                      level_shift = mean(yte) - mean(ytr),
                      r2_linear=r2_lin, r2_enet=r2_enet, r2_xgb=r2_xgb,
                      r2_linear_centred = r2_cent,
                      flexibility_gain = r2_xgb - r2_lin,
                      best_iter = bst$best_iteration),
       model=bst, Xte=Xte, yte=yte,
       # Retained for F26 (the learning curve) and F28 (predicted vs. observed).
       # Without this the model would need refitting purely to plot it.
       eval_log = as.data.table(bst$evaluation_log),
       pred_xgb = as.numeric(predict(bst, Xte)),
       pred_lin = pred_lin)
}

RES <- lapply(names(SPL), function(nm) run_split(nm, SPL[[nm]]))
names(RES) <- names(SPL)
RES <- RES[!sapply(RES, is.null)]
VALID <- rbindlist(lapply(RES, `[[`, "row"))
fwrite(VALID, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T16_predictive_validation.csv"))

SHIFT_S <- {
  worst <- VALID[which.min(r2_linear)]
  sprintf("Out-of-sample performance varies sharply across the four designs. The %s design returns the weakest transfer (linear out-of-sample R-squared %.3f), but decomposing that error shows the held-out group's mean life evaluation differs from the training group's by %.2f Cantril points; once that level offset is removed the same predictions return an R-squared of %.3f. The failure is therefore substantially one of calibration across contexts rather than of the predictors carrying no signal, and it is reported as such: the catalogue's associations do not transport unchanged across development levels, which is itself consistent with the development-graded heterogeneity documented in Section 3.8.",
    worst$design, worst$r2_linear, worst$level_shift, worst$r2_linear_centred)
}
message(SHIFT_S)

FUNCFORM <- list(
  gain_country = VALID[design=="country", flexibility_gain],
  gain_random  = VALID[design=="random",  flexibility_gain],
  gap_designs  = VALID[design=="random", r2_xgb] - VALID[design=="country", r2_xgb])
# If the country holdout goes negative for BOTH model classes, the honest
# reading is that country-level predictors do not transport to unseen
# countries at all - report that rather than a flexibility gain.
FUNCFORM$transports <- VALID[design=="country", r2_linear] > 0

# Braces on both branches: `else` cannot begin a top-level line in R.
gap_abs <- abs(FUNCFORM$gap_designs)
gap_reading <- if (gap_abs < 0.01) {
  "little evidence of a random-split advantage over the unseen-country test"
} else if (gap_abs < 0.03) {
  "a modest difference between interpolation and transfer to unseen countries"
} else {
  "a substantial deterioration from interpolation to transfer across countries"
}

FUNCFORM$sentence <- if (!isTRUE(FUNCFORM$transports)) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("On the country-block holdout the linear and boosted models return ",
           "out-of-sample R-squared values of %.3f and %.3f. Because performance ",
           "is below zero, the catalogue does not predict unseen countries better ",
           "than their own mean. The random-split boosted result is %.3f, a design ",
           "difference of %.3f; this indicates %s. The two model families fail ",
           "together, providing no evidence that flexible functional form repairs ",
           "the transport problem."),
    VALID[design=="country", r2_linear], VALID[design=="country", r2_xgb],
    VALID[design=="random", r2_xgb], FUNCFORM$gap_designs, gap_reading)
} else if (FUNCFORM$gain_country <= 0) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("On the country-block holdout, gradient boosting underperforms the ",
           "linear specification by %.3f out-of-sample R-squared points (%.3f ",
           "versus %.3f). Flexibility therefore recovers no additional signal on ",
           "unseen countries, providing no indication that the CRE coefficients ",
           "are crude approximations to a materially non-linear surface. The ",
           "boosted random-split minus country-holdout difference is %.3f, ",
           "indicating %s."),
    abs(FUNCFORM$gain_country),
    VALID[design=="country", r2_xgb],
    VALID[design=="country", r2_linear],
    FUNCFORM$gap_designs, gap_reading)
} else {
  sprintf(
    paste0("On the country-block holdout, gradient boosting improves out-of-sample ",
           "R-squared over the linear specification by %.3f. This recovers %s ",
           "predictive signal, so the CRE coefficients are %s treated as crude ",
           "approximations to a materially non-linear surface. The boosted random-",
           "split minus country-holdout difference is %.3f, indicating %s."),
    FUNCFORM$gain_country,
    ifelse(FUNCFORM$gain_country < 0.02, "little additional", "meaningful additional"),
    ifelse(FUNCFORM$gain_country < 0.02, "not", "better"),
    FUNCFORM$gap_designs, gap_reading)
}

## ---- LEVEL-SEPARATED PERMUTATION IMPORTANCE ----
# >>> FIX (reproducibility audit): if every design in run_split() fails its
# minimum-row guard (line ~2265; happens under QUICK = TRUE with a small
# n_max), RES ends up completely empty. Without this check, `names(RES)[1]`
# silently becomes NA and `RES[[NA]]` throws a raw, unguarded R error --
# this is not wrapped in tryCatch, so it takes down every downstream object
# with it (PI feeds Table 4, Table 5, and several figures) with no graceful
# "skipped" message, just a dead session. This is very likely the root cause
# of earlier renders that stopped mid-file with no visible error. <<<
if (length(RES) == 0L) {
  stop("Every predictive-validation design (random/country/temporal/",
       "development) returned NULL from run_split() -- RES is empty. ",
       "This happens under QUICK = TRUE when CFG$n_max is too small for ",
       "one or more splits to clear their minimum-row guard (>=100 test, ",
       ">=500 train rows). Increase CFG$n_max, or set QUICK = FALSE, before ",
       "re-running this chunk. (Everything above this point in the pipeline ",
       "is unaffected and does not need to be re-run.)")
}
perm_importance <- function(bst, X, y, feats, reps=if(CFG$QUICK) 3 else 10) {
  base <- r2_oos(y, predict(bst, X))
  rbindlist(lapply(feats, function(f) {
    drops <- replicate(reps, {
      Xp <- X; Xp[,f] <- sample(Xp[,f])
      base - r2_oos(y, predict(bst, Xp))
    })
    data.table(feature=f, importance=mean(drops), sd=sd(drops))
  }))
}
key <- if ("country" %in% names(RES)) "country" else names(RES)[1]
PI <- perm_importance(RES[[key]]$model, RES[[key]]$Xte, RES[[key]]$yte, FEATS)
PI[, level := fifelse(grepl("_w$",feature),"within",
              fifelse(grepl("_b$",feature),"between","missing flag"))]
PI[, code := gsub("_(w|b|miss)$","",feature)]
PI <- merge(PI, CAT[, .(code,label,domain)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
PI[code=="ln_gdp", `:=`(label="GDP per capita (log)", domain="Income")]
fwrite(PI, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T17_permutation_importance.csv"))

gdp_w_rank <- PI[level=="within"][order(-importance)][, which(code=="ln_gdp")]
gdp_b_rank <- PI[level=="between"][order(-importance)][, which(code=="ln_gdp")]
LEVELCONF <- sprintf(
  "Read at the between-country level, GDP per capita ranks %d of %d features by permutation importance; read at the within-country level it ranks %d of %d. Because the two components enter the boosted model as distinct features, this contrast demonstrates rather than asserts that an analyst using the raw, undecomposed variable would attribute a cross-national regularity to within-country change.",
  gdp_b_rank, PI[level=="between", .N], gdp_w_rank, PI[level=="within", .N])

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 14b: THREE-LEVEL ML SATELLITE  (respondent level added)
# ============================================================================
# WHY THIS IS A SATELLITE AND NOT A REPLACEMENT.
# The main ML model above (Section 14) uses only country-year features, and
# its permutation importance is what LEVELCONF/Proposition 2 rest on. This
# block re-runs the SAME flexible model with a THIRD feature added -- the
# respondent's own income position relative to same-country-year peers -- and
# reports it separately, so the headline level-conflation result is unchanged
# and directly comparable to a version that includes the individual level.
#
# SCOPE (critical). The GWP is a repeated cross-section: a different sample of
# roughly a thousand people is drawn per country-year and no respondent is
# observed twice. The respondent-level feature is therefore a SAME-MOMENT
# comparison between different people, never a within-person change.
#
# CONTAMINATION. Only ln_income_h is taken to the respondent level. Evaluative
# items (pain, satisfaction, perceived safety) are deliberately NOT, because a
# respondent reports predictor and outcome in the same interview and shared
# momentary state would inflate their association -- the same-method bias the
# country-year averaging in the main model washes out but an N=1 comparison
# cannot. INCOME_5 is also excluded: it is a Gallup-constructed within-country
# quintile, so its country-year mean is constant by construction.
ML3 <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("DT_IND"), "ln_income_h" %in% names(DT_IND))

  d3 <- DT_IND[, .(iso3, year, wt, ln_income_h)]
  d3[, grp_mean := weighted.mean(ln_income_h, wt, na.rm=TRUE), by=.(iso3, year)]
  d3[, ln_income_h_p := ln_income_h - grp_mean]

  # Rebuilds the ML frame with the SAME recipe as MLD, plus the new feature.
  # Rebuilt from DT/CY rather than joined onto MLD because ANA reorders rows when
  # to merge on and does not retain a respondent id to align by.
  d3_slim <- d3[, .(iso3, year, wt, ln_income_h_p)]
  d3_slim <- d3_slim[!is.na(ln_income_h_p)]
  base3 <- DT_IND[, c("iso3","year", OUTCOME), with=FALSE]
  setnames(base3, OUTCOME, "cantril")
  stopifnot(nrow(base3) == nrow(DT_IND))
  base3[, ln_income_h_p := d3$ln_income_h_p]     # misma fila, DT_IND sin reordenar
  base3[, wt := DT_IND$wt]

  MLD3 <- merge(base3,
                CY[, c("iso3","year", W_VARS, B_VARS, M_VARS), with=FALSE],
                by=c("iso3","year"))
  gdp_terc3 <- unique(ANA[, .(iso3, dev_stratum)])
  MLD3 <- merge(MLD3, gdp_terc3, by="iso3", all.x=TRUE)
  FEATS3 <- c(FEATS, "ln_income_h_p")
  MLD3 <- MLD3[complete.cases(MLD3[, c("cantril","wt","dev_stratum", FEATS3), with=FALSE])]
  stopifnot(nrow(MLD3) > 1000)

  SPL3 <- make_splits(MLD3)
  key3  <- "country"            # the serious design: countries never seen in training
  sp3   <- SPL3[[key3]]
  Xtr3 <- as.matrix(MLD3[sp3$tr, ..FEATS3]); ytr3 <- MLD3$cantril[sp3$tr]
  Xte3 <- as.matrix(MLD3[sp3$te, ..FEATS3]); yte3 <- MLD3$cantril[sp3$te]

  bst3 <- xgboost::xgb.train(
    params=list(objective="reg:squarederror", eta=if(CFG$QUICK) 0.1 else 0.05,
                max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8,
                nthread=1, seed=CFG$seed),   # deterministic: see note on bst
    data=xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(Xtr3, label=ytr3),
    nrounds=if(CFG$QUICK) 400 else CFG$xgb_rounds_max,
    watchlist=list(val=xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(Xte3, label=yte3)),
    early_stopping_rounds=CFG$xgb_early_stop, verbose=0)

  r2_xgb3 <- r2_oos(yte3, predict(bst3, Xte3))
  PI3 <- perm_importance(bst3, Xte3, yte3, FEATS3)
  PI3[, level := fifelse(feature=="ln_income_h_p", "respondent",
                  fifelse(grepl("_w$",feature),"within",
                  fifelse(grepl("_b$",feature),"between","missing flag")))]
  setorder(PI3, -importance)
  PI3[, rank_overall := .I]
  fwrite(PI3, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T27_ml_three_level_importance.csv"))

  rank_p  <- PI3[feature=="ln_income_h_p", rank_overall][1]
  n_feat3 <- nrow(PI3)
  best_w  <- PI3[level=="within"][order(-importance)][1]
  best_b  <- PI3[level=="between"][order(-importance)][1]

  ML3_S <- sprintf(
    "Adding the respondent's own income position relative to same-country-year peers as a third-level feature to the flexible model places it %d of %d features by permutation importance on the country holdout, against %s (%s) as the strongest within-country feature and %s (%s) as the strongest between-country one. Out-of-sample R-squared on unseen countries is %.3f. Because the Gallup World Poll is a repeated cross-section, this feature compares different respondents surveyed at the same time rather than the same respondent over time, and only the household income measure is taken to respondent level: evaluative items are excluded because a respondent reports predictor and outcome in a single interview, so shared momentary state would inflate their association where country-year averaging cannot wash it out. The result is reported alongside, not instead of, the country-year model of Section 3.9, so the level-conflation contrast above is unaffected.",
    rank_p, n_feat3,
    if (nrow(best_w)) best_w$label[1] else "n/a", if (nrow(best_w)) best_w$feature[1] else "n/a",
    if (nrow(best_b)) best_b$label[1] else "n/a", if (nrow(best_b)) best_b$feature[1] else "n/a",
    r2_xgb3)
  message(ML3_S)
  list(pi=PI3, r2=r2_xgb3, rank_respondent=rank_p, sentence=ML3_S)
}, error=function(e){
  message("Three-level ML satellite skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL
})

```



```{r individual_battery}
#| cache: false
# >>> INDIVIDUAL_BATTERY_V27_START >>>
# ============================================================================
# SECTION 14c: RESPONDENT-LEVEL INEQUALITY AND PRE-SPECIFIED HETEROGENEITY
# ============================================================================
# PURPOSE AND ESTIMAND.
# The CRE-Mundlak model answers two contextual questions: what distinguishes
# countries, and what moves when a country changes. This section answers the
# third question without conflating it with either of those: among respondents
# interviewed in the SAME country and year, which structural characteristics
# are associated with reporting a higher life evaluation?
#
# Country-year fixed effects absorb every observed and unobserved characteristic
# shared by respondents in that country-year. The coefficients therefore compare
# people exposed to the same national context and common survey wave. They are
# adjusted associations, not causal effects and not within-person change: Gallup
# is a repeated cross-section and does not follow the same respondent over time.
#
# SCOPE DISCIPLINE.
# Only structural respondent characteristics enter: relative household income,
# demographics, urbanity, family composition and employment. Contemporaneous
# perceptions, affect and satisfaction items are excluded to avoid same-interview
# common-method contamination. Heterogeneity is pre-specified for the relative-
# income slope, the one substantive respondent-level estimand, rather than testing
# every coefficient against every subgroup after seeing the results.

INDIVIDUAL <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("ANA"), exists("CFG"), exists("OUTCOME"))
  if (!requireNamespace("fixest", quietly=TRUE))
    stop("Package 'fixest' is required for the respondent-level battery.")

  # ---- minimal respondent frame: country-year FE means national W/B columns
  # are neither needed nor duplicated in memory.
  ind_keep <- unique(c(
    "cantril", "wt", "iso3", "year", "cy", "dev_stratum",
    "ln_income_h", "WP1220", "age_c", "sex_f", "educ_f", "urban_f",
    "marital_f", "children_n", "EMP_LFPR", "EMP_FTEMP_POP",
    "EMP_WORK_HOURS", "INCOME_5"
  ))
  ind_keep <- intersect(ind_keep, names(ANA))
  IND <- copy(ANA[, ..ind_keep])
  stopifnot(all(c("cantril","wt","iso3","year","cy") %in% names(IND)))
  IND <- IND[is.finite(cantril) & is.finite(wt) & wt > 0]
  if (nrow(IND) < 1000L) stop("Respondent frame has fewer than 1,000 usable observations.")

  IND[, `:=`(
    iso3 = factor(as.character(iso3)),
    cy   = factor(as.character(cy))
  )]

  # ---- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------
  explicit_missing <- function(x, label="Missing / not reported") {
    z <- as.character(x)
    z[is.na(z) | !nzchar(trimws(z)) | z %in% c("NA","<NA>")] <- label
    factor(z)
  }

  wmean_safe <- function(x, w) {
    ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
    if (sum(ok) < 2L || sum(w[ok]) <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    weighted.mean(x[ok], w[ok])
  }
  wsd_safe <- function(x, w) {
    ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
    if (sum(ok) < 3L || sum(w[ok]) <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    mu <- weighted.mean(x[ok], w[ok])
    s <- sqrt(sum(w[ok] * (x[ok] - mu)^2) / sum(w[ok]))
    if (!is.finite(s) || s < 1e-8) NA_real_ else s
  }
  valid_factor <- function(x, min_n=500L) {
    z <- droplevels(factor(x))
    tab <- table(z, useNA="no")
    length(tab) >= 2L && sum(tab >= min_n) >= 2L
  }
  valid_numeric <- function(x) {
    z <- as.numeric(x)
    sum(is.finite(z)) >= 1000L && is.finite(sd(z, na.rm=TRUE)) && sd(z, na.rm=TRUE) > 1e-8
  }

  # ---- relative household income: standardized inside each country-year ------
  if ("ln_income_h" %in% names(IND)) {
    IND[, c(".inc_mu", ".inc_sd") := .(
      wmean_safe(ln_income_h, wt), wsd_safe(ln_income_h, wt)
    ), by=cy]
    IND[, income_rel_z := (ln_income_h - .inc_mu) / .inc_sd]
    IND[, c(".inc_mu", ".inc_sd") := NULL]
  } else IND[, income_rel_z := NA_real_]
  IND[, income_rel_missing := as.integer(!is.finite(income_rel_z))]
  IND[!is.finite(income_rel_z), income_rel_z := 0]
  # Winsorisation is only a robustness guard; with a z-score, it affects tails.
  q_inc <- quantile(IND[income_rel_missing==0, income_rel_z], c(.01,.99), na.rm=TRUE)
  if (length(q_inc)==2L && all(is.finite(q_inc)))
    IND[, income_rel_z_w := pmin(pmax(income_rel_z, q_inc[1]), q_inc[2])]
  else IND[, income_rel_z_w := income_rel_z]
  IND[, income_rel_z2 := income_rel_z_w^2]

  # ---- age bands: interpretable and flexible without a high-degree polynomial --
  if ("WP1220" %in% names(IND)) {
    age_raw <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(IND$WP1220))
  } else if ("age_c" %in% names(IND)) {
    # age_c is globally centred; recover ordering, not an absolute age label.
    age_raw <- as.numeric(IND$age_c)
  } else age_raw <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(IND))

  if ("WP1220" %in% names(IND)) {
    IND[, age_band := cut(age_raw,
      breaks=c(-Inf,24,34,44,54,64,Inf),
      labels=c("15-24","25-34","35-44","45-54","55-64","65+"),
      right=TRUE)]
  } else {
    qq <- unique(quantile(age_raw, probs=seq(0,1,length.out=7), na.rm=TRUE))
    IND[, age_band := if (length(qq) >= 3L) cut(age_raw, qq, include.lowest=TRUE) else factor(NA)]
  }
  IND[, age_band := explicit_missing(age_band)]
  if ("25-34" %in% levels(IND$age_band)) IND[, age_band := relevel(age_band, "25-34")]

  # ---- education: collapse the standard Gallup three-level code when possible -
  if ("educ_f" %in% names(IND)) {
    ed_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(IND$educ_f)))
    if (mean(is.finite(ed_num)) > .5 && all(na.omit(unique(ed_num)) %in% 1:3)) {
      IND[, educ3 := factor(fcase(
        ed_num == 1, "Primary or less",
        ed_num == 2, "Secondary",
        ed_num == 3, "Tertiary",
        default=NA_character_),
        levels=c("Secondary","Primary or less","Tertiary"))]
    } else IND[, educ3 := explicit_missing(educ_f)]
  } else IND[, educ3 := factor("Missing / not reported")]
  IND[, educ3 := explicit_missing(educ3)]
  if ("Secondary" %in% levels(IND$educ3)) IND[, educ3 := relevel(educ3, "Secondary")]

  # ---- remaining demographic factors ----------------------------------------
  for (v in intersect(c("sex_f","urban_f","marital_f"), names(IND)))
    set(IND, j=v, value=explicit_missing(IND[[v]]))
  if ("sex_f" %in% names(IND) && "male" %in% levels(IND$sex_f))
    IND[, sex_f := relevel(sex_f, "male")]

  if ("children_n" %in% names(IND)) {
    IND[, .child_mu := wmean_safe(as.numeric(children_n), wt), by=cy]
    IND[, children_cy := as.numeric(children_n) - .child_mu]
    IND[, .child_mu := NULL]
  } else IND[, children_cy := NA_real_]
  IND[, children_missing := as.integer(!is.finite(children_cy))]
  IND[!is.finite(children_cy), children_cy := 0]

  # ---- one mutually exclusive employment factor avoids nested binary terms ----
  lf <- if ("EMP_LFPR" %in% names(IND)) as.numeric(IND$EMP_LFPR) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(IND))
  pe <- if ("EMP_FTEMP_POP" %in% names(IND)) as.numeric(IND$EMP_FTEMP_POP) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(IND))
  IND[, employment3 := factor(fcase(
    pe == 1, "Payroll employed",
    lf == 1, "In labour force, not payroll",
    lf == 0, "Out of labour force",
    default="Missing / not reported"),
    levels=c("Out of labour force","In labour force, not payroll","Payroll employed","Missing / not reported"))]

  # Worker-hours sensitivity only; not in the main model because it is undefined
  # for non-workers and would change the estimand and analytical population.
  if ("EMP_WORK_HOURS" %in% names(IND)) {
    IND[, work_hours := suppressWarnings(as.numeric(EMP_WORK_HOURS))]
    IND[work_hours < 0 | work_hours > 98, work_hours := NA_real_]
    IND[, c(".hrs_mu", ".hrs_sd") := .(
      wmean_safe(work_hours, wt), wsd_safe(work_hours, wt)
    ), by=cy]
    IND[, work_hours_rel_z := (work_hours - .hrs_mu) / .hrs_sd]
    IND[, c(".hrs_mu", ".hrs_sd") := NULL]
  } else IND[, work_hours_rel_z := NA_real_]

  # ---- contextual moderators for transportability ----------------------------
  if (!"dev_stratum" %in% names(IND) && exists("ANA") && "dev_stratum" %in% names(ANA)) {
    ds <- unique(ANA[, .(iso3=as.character(iso3), dev_stratum)])
    IND[, iso3_chr := as.character(iso3)]
    IND <- merge(IND, ds, by.x="iso3_chr", by.y="iso3", all.x=TRUE, sort=FALSE)
    IND[, iso3_chr := NULL]
  }
  if ("dev_stratum" %in% names(IND)) IND[, dev_stratum := explicit_missing(dev_stratum)]

  if (requireNamespace("countrycode", quietly=TRUE)) {
    IND[, wb_region := countrycode::countrycode(
      as.character(iso3), origin="iso3c", destination="region", nomatch=NA_character_)]
    IND[, wb_region := explicit_missing(wb_region)]
  } else {
    warning("countrycode not installed: regional heterogeneity will be recorded as unavailable.")
    IND[, wb_region := factor("Unavailable")]
  }

  # ---- model terms selected only when identified ------------------------------
  demographic_candidates <- c("age_band","sex_f","educ3","urban_f","marital_f",
                              "children_cy","children_missing")
  resource_candidates <- c("income_rel_z_w","income_rel_missing","employment3")
  keep_term <- function(v) {
    if (!v %in% names(IND)) return(FALSE)
    if (is.factor(IND[[v]]) || is.character(IND[[v]])) valid_factor(IND[[v]]) else valid_numeric(IND[[v]])
  }
  demo_terms <- demographic_candidates[vapply(demographic_candidates, keep_term, logical(1))]
  resource_terms <- resource_candidates[vapply(resource_candidates, keep_term, logical(1))]
  if (!"income_rel_z_w" %in% resource_terms)
    stop("Relative household income has insufficient within-country-year variation.")
  full_terms <- unique(c(demo_terms, resource_terms))

  # One common sample for nested model comparison; explicit missing categories
  # and flags prevent listwise deletion from silently redefining the population.
  common_vars <- unique(c("cantril","wt","iso3","cy",full_terms))
  D <- IND[complete.cases(IND[, ..common_vars])]
  if (nrow(D) < 5000L || uniqueN(D$iso3) < 20L || uniqueN(D$cy) < 50L)
    stop("Individual model lacks minimum support: ", nrow(D), " rows, ",
         uniqueN(D$iso3), " countries, ", uniqueN(D$cy), " country-years.")

  rhs <- function(x) if (length(x)) paste(x, collapse=" + ") else "1"
  f0 <- as.formula("cantril ~ 1 | cy")
  fd <- as.formula(paste0("cantril ~ ", rhs(demo_terms), " | cy"))
  ff <- as.formula(paste0("cantril ~ ", rhs(full_terms), " | cy"))
  fn <- as.formula(paste0("cantril ~ ", rhs(c(full_terms,"income_rel_z2")), " | cy"))

  # Country-clustered SEs allow arbitrary dependence among respondents and waves
  # within the same country. Country-year FE absorb all shared wave-level context.
  M0 <- fixest::feols(f0, data=D, weights=~wt, vcov=~iso3, notes=FALSE)
  MD <- fixest::feols(fd, data=D, weights=~wt, vcov=~iso3, notes=FALSE)
  MF <- fixest::feols(ff, data=D, weights=~wt, vcov=~iso3, notes=FALSE)
  MN <- fixest::feols(fn, data=D, weights=~wt, vcov=~iso3, notes=FALSE)

  r2row <- function(m, model, question) {
    rr <- tryCatch(
      fixest::r2(m, type=c("wr2","war2")),
      error=function(e) c(wr2=0, war2=NA_real_)
    )
    wr2 <- unname(rr["wr2"]); war2 <- unname(rr["war2"])
    if (!length(wr2) || !is.finite(wr2)) wr2 <- 0
    if (!length(war2) || !is.finite(war2)) war2 <- NA_real_
    data.table(model=model, question=question, n=stats::nobs(m),
      n_countries=uniqueN(D$iso3), n_country_years=uniqueN(D$cy),
      within_r2=wr2, adjusted_within_r2=war2)
  }
  MODEL_COMPARISON <- rbindlist(list(
    r2row(M0, "Country-year context only", "How much respondent variance remains before individual information?"),
    r2row(MD, "Demographic composition", "How much do observed demographic differences add?"),
    r2row(MF, "Full structural respondent model", "How much do income and employment add beyond composition?"),
    r2row(MN, "Non-linear income sensitivity", "Does a quadratic income gradient improve the respondent account?")
  ))
  MODEL_COMPARISON[, incremental_within_r2 := within_r2 - shift(within_r2, fill=within_r2[1])]
  # >>> THESIS Table 6 ("Respondent-Level Explanatory Fit Within Country-Year") -- HIGH confidence <<<
  fwrite(MODEL_COMPARISON, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T28_individual_model_comparison.csv"))

  # ---- coefficient table with clustered inference ----------------------------
  ct <- as.data.table(fixest::coeftable(MF), keep.rownames="term")
  setnames(ct, names(ct), c("term","estimate","std.error","statistic","p.value"))
  ct[, `:=`(
    conf.low  = estimate - qt(.975, df=max(1, uniqueN(D$iso3)-1)) * std.error,
    conf.high = estimate + qt(.975, df=max(1, uniqueN(D$iso3)-1)) * std.error,
    family="respondent_main")]
  ct[, p_fdr := p.adjust(p.value, method="BH")]
  ct[, sig_fdr := p_fdr < CFG$fdr_alpha]

  label_term <- function(z) {
    z <- gsub("income_rel_z_w", "Relative household income (1 SD within country-year)", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("income_rel_missing", "Household income missing", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("income_rel_z2", "Relative household income squared", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("children_cy", "Children under 15 (within-country-year centred)", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("children_missing", "Number of children missing", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("age_band", "Age: ", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("sex_f", "Sex: ", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("educ3", "Education: ", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("urban_f", "Settlement: ", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("marital_f", "Marital status: ", z, fixed=TRUE)
    z <- gsub("employment3", "Employment: ", z, fixed=TRUE)
    gsub("_", " ", z, fixed=TRUE)
  }
  ct[, label := vapply(term, label_term, character(1))]
  fwrite(ct, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T29_individual_coefficients.csv"))

  # ---- nonlinear income test --------------------------------------------------
  wnl <- fixest::wald(MN, keep="income_rel_z2", cluster=~iso3, print=FALSE)
  NONLINEAR <- data.table(
    term="income_rel_z2",
    statistic=if (length(wnl)) unname(wnl["stat"]) else NA_real_,
    p.value=if (length(wnl)) unname(wnl["p"]) else NA_real_)
  fwrite(NONLINEAR, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T30_individual_income_nonlinearity.csv"))

  # ---- worker-hours sensitivity ----------------------------------------------
  WORK_HOURS <- NULL
  if (valid_numeric(IND$work_hours_rel_z)) {
    Dw <- IND[is.finite(work_hours_rel_z) & employment3 != "Out of labour force"]
    if (nrow(Dw) >= 3000L && uniqueN(Dw$iso3) >= 20L) {
      fwh <- as.formula(paste0("cantril ~ work_hours_rel_z + ", rhs(full_terms), " | cy"))
      MWH <- fixest::feols(fwh, data=Dw, weights=~wt, vcov=~iso3, notes=FALSE)
      wh <- as.data.table(fixest::coeftable(MWH), keep.rownames="term")[term=="work_hours_rel_z"]
      if (nrow(wh)) {
        setnames(wh, names(wh), c("term","estimate","std.error","statistic","p.value"))
        wh[, `:=`(n=nrow(Dw), n_countries=uniqueN(Dw$iso3),
                   conf.low=estimate-1.96*std.error, conf.high=estimate+1.96*std.error)]
        WORK_HOURS <- wh
        fwrite(WORK_HOURS, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T31_worker_hours_sensitivity.csv"))
      }
      rm(MWH); invisible(gc())
    }
  }

  # ---- pre-specified heterogeneity battery -----------------------------------
  # Formal interaction tests answer whether the relative-income slope differs
  # across groups. Group-specific slopes are linear combinations from the same
  # interaction model, not unrelated regressions run on different specifications.
  MODS <- list(
    sex       = list(var="sex_f",       label="Sex"),
    age       = list(var="age_band",    label="Age"),
    education = list(var="educ3",       label="Education"),
    urbanity  = list(var="urban_f",     label="Urban / rural settlement"),
    marital   = list(var="marital_f",   label="Marital status"),
    employment= list(var="employment3",label="Employment status"),
    development=list(var="dev_stratum",label="Development stratum"),
    region    = list(var="wb_region",   label="World Bank region")
  )

  slope_from_model <- function(m, mod, lev, ref, dmod) {
    b <- coef(m)
    V <- stats::vcov(m, cluster=~iso3)
    if (!"income_rel_z_w" %in% names(b)) return(NULL)
    cvec <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b)); cvec["income_rel_z_w"] <- 1
    if (!identical(as.character(lev), as.character(ref))) {
      target <- paste0(mod, lev)
      cand <- names(b)[grepl("income_rel_z_w", names(b), fixed=TRUE) &
                       grepl(target, names(b), fixed=TRUE)]
      if (!length(cand)) {
        target2 <- paste0(mod, make.names(lev))
        cand <- names(b)[grepl("income_rel_z_w", names(b), fixed=TRUE) &
                         grepl(target2, names(b), fixed=TRUE)]
      }
      if (!length(cand)) return(NULL)
      cvec[cand[1]] <- 1
    }
    est <- sum(cvec*b)
    se  <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(cvec) %*% V %*% cvec))
    sup <- dmod[get(mod)==lev, .(n=.N, n_countries=uniqueN(iso3), n_country_years=uniqueN(cy))]
    data.table(group=as.character(lev), reference=as.character(ref),
      estimate=est, std.error=se, conf.low=est-1.96*se, conf.high=est+1.96*se,
      n=sup$n, n_countries=sup$n_countries, n_country_years=sup$n_country_years)
  }

  HET_SLOPES <- list(); HET_TESTS <- list(); SUPPORT <- list()
  for (nm in names(MODS)) {
    mod <- MODS[[nm]]$var; mlab <- MODS[[nm]]$label
    if (!mod %in% names(IND) || !valid_factor(IND[[mod]], min_n=750L)) {
      SUPPORT[[nm]] <- data.table(moderator=mlab, variable=mod, status="Unavailable or insufficient variation")
      next
    }
    dsup <- IND[, .(n=.N, n_countries=uniqueN(iso3), n_country_years=uniqueN(cy)), by=mod]
    ok_levels <- dsup[n >= 750L & n_countries >= 15L & n_country_years >= 30L &
      !grepl("missing|unavailable|not reported", as.character(get(mod)), ignore.case=TRUE), get(mod)]
    if (length(ok_levels) < 2L) {
      SUPPORT[[nm]] <- data.table(moderator=mlab, variable=mod,
        status="Fewer than two adequately supported groups")
      next
    }
    dmod <- IND[get(mod) %in% ok_levels]
    dmod[, (mod) := droplevels(factor(get(mod)))]
    ref <- levels(dmod[[mod]])[1]
    # Keep the common structural controls and add the moderator main effect if it
    # is contextual and therefore absent from the main respondent formula.
    terms0 <- unique(c(full_terms, mod))
    terms0 <- setdiff(terms0, "income_rel_z_w")
    fhet <- as.formula(paste0(
      "cantril ~ income_rel_z_w + ", rhs(terms0),
      " + income_rel_z_w:", mod, " | cy"))
    needh <- unique(c("cantril","wt","iso3","cy","income_rel_z_w",terms0,mod))
    dmod <- dmod[complete.cases(dmod[, ..needh])]
    if (nrow(dmod) < 3000L || uniqueN(dmod$iso3) < 15L) next

    mh <- tryCatch(fixest::feols(fhet, data=dmod, weights=~wt, vcov=~iso3, notes=FALSE),
                   error=function(e) { message("Heterogeneity ", nm, " skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
    if (is.null(mh)) next
    pat <- paste0("income_rel_z_w:.*", mod, "|", mod, ".*:income_rel_z_w")
    ww <- fixest::wald(mh, keep=pat, cluster=~iso3, print=FALSE)
    HET_TESTS[[nm]] <- data.table(
      moderator=mlab, variable=mod,
      statistic=if (length(ww)) unname(ww["stat"]) else NA_real_,
      p.value=if (length(ww)) unname(ww["p"]) else NA_real_,
      df1=if (length(ww)) unname(ww["df1"]) else NA_real_,
      df2=if (length(ww)) unname(ww["df2"]) else NA_real_)
    sl <- rbindlist(lapply(levels(dmod[[mod]]), function(lv)
      slope_from_model(mh, mod, lv, ref, dmod)), fill=TRUE)
    if (nrow(sl)) {
      sl[, `:=`(moderator=mlab, variable=mod)]
      HET_SLOPES[[nm]] <- sl
    }
    SUPPORT[[nm]] <- dsup[, .(moderator=mlab, variable=mod, group=get(mod),
                              n, n_countries, n_country_years,
                              status=fifelse(get(mod) %in% ok_levels,"Estimated","Insufficient support"))]
    rm(mh); invisible(gc())
  }

  HET_TESTS <- if (length(HET_TESTS)) rbindlist(HET_TESTS, fill=TRUE) else data.table()
  if (nrow(HET_TESTS)) {
    HET_TESTS[, p_fdr := p.adjust(p.value, method="BH")]
    HET_TESTS[, heterogeneous_fdr := p_fdr < CFG$fdr_alpha]
  }
  HET_SLOPES <- if (length(HET_SLOPES)) rbindlist(HET_SLOPES, fill=TRUE) else data.table()
  if (nrow(HET_SLOPES) && nrow(HET_TESTS))
    HET_SLOPES <- merge(HET_SLOPES,
      HET_TESTS[, .(moderator, p_omnibus=p.value, p_fdr_omnibus=p_fdr, heterogeneous_fdr)],
      by="moderator", all.x=TRUE)
  SUPPORT <- if (length(SUPPORT)) rbindlist(SUPPORT, fill=TRUE) else data.table()

  fwrite(HET_TESTS,  file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T32_individual_heterogeneity_tests.csv"))
  fwrite(HET_SLOPES, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T33_individual_group_slopes.csv"))
  fwrite(SUPPORT,    file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T34_individual_support_audit.csv"))

  # ---- estimand register: makes the third level impossible to misread ---------
  ESTIMAND_REGISTER <- data.table(
    component=c("Individual main model","Relative-income slope","Heterogeneity battery","Worker-hours sensitivity"),
    comparison=c(
      "Different respondents in the same country-year",
      "One-SD difference in household-income position among contemporaneous compatriots",
      "Difference in that same respondent-level slope across pre-specified groups",
      "Difference in hours among workers observed in the same country-year"),
    adjustment=c(
      "Country-year fixed effects; demographics, family composition and employment; country-clustered SE",
      "Same full respondent model",
      "Same full model plus formal interactions; FDR across moderator families",
      "Worker-only sample; same structural controls and country-year fixed effects"),
    supports=c(
      "Adjusted cross-sectional association at respondent level",
      "Relative-position association",
      "Effect-pattern heterogeneity, not causal treatment-effect heterogeneity",
      "Descriptive worker-hours sensitivity"),
    does_not_support=c(
      "Within-person change or causal effects",
      "An income intervention effect",
      "Post-treatment subgroup claims or person-specific effects",
      "A labour-supply causal interpretation"))
  fwrite(ESTIMAND_REGISTER, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T35_individual_estimand_register.csv"))

  n_het <- if (nrow(HET_TESTS)) sum(HET_TESTS$heterogeneous_fdr, na.rm=TRUE) else 0L
  gain_demo <- MODEL_COMPARISON[model=="Demographic composition", within_r2] - MODEL_COMPARISON[1, within_r2]
  gain_full <- MODEL_COMPARISON[model=="Full structural respondent model", within_r2] - MODEL_COMPARISON[1, within_r2]
  INDIVIDUAL_S <- sprintf(
    paste0("Holding constant every characteristic shared within a country-year, observed demographic composition adds %.3f to within-country-year R-squared and the full structural respondent model adds %.3f. The relative-income gradient is estimated with country-clustered uncertainty and tested across %d pre-specified moderators; %d remain heterogeneous after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. These are comparisons between different respondents interviewed in the same national context, not changes within the same person and not causal effects."),
    gain_demo, gain_full, nrow(HET_TESTS), n_het)
  message(INDIVIDUAL_S)

  # Models are deliberately not returned or saved: the tables contain everything
  # the figures and dissertation need, while avoiding a multi-GB cache object.
  out <- list(
    model_comparison=MODEL_COMPARISON,
    coefficients=ct,
    nonlinearity=NONLINEAR,
    worker_hours=WORK_HOURS,
    heterogeneity_tests=HET_TESTS,
    group_slopes=HET_SLOPES,
    support=SUPPORT,
    estimand_register=ESTIMAND_REGISTER,
    sentence=INDIVIDUAL_S,
    n=nrow(D), n_countries=uniqueN(D$iso3), n_country_years=uniqueN(D$cy)
  )
  rm(M0,MD,MF,MN,D,IND); invisible(gc())
  out
}, error=function(e) {
  message("Respondent-level battery skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
  NULL
})

# ---- PRE-FIGURE STATE: resume figures without re-running models ---------------
# This directly fixes the failure mode encountered in v26: figures depended on
# temporary objects that existed only in memory. Save every compact object needed
# for the visual/reporting stage before entering that stage.
.prefig_names <- c(
  "CFG","CAT","COEF","DOM","DOM_TIPO","DOM_ITEM","DOMINANCE_TIPO",
  "OSTER","LEADLAG","HET_DEV","GRAD","PI","PI3","VALID","MODEL_AB",
  "REL","LOAD","IMP_TAB","IMP_PROS","SCOPE","REFSENS","VARACC","ICC",
  "Q1","Q2","FDR","FACTOR","ML3","MUNDLAK","DIRAUDIT","SIGN_DX",
  "CMP_CTRL","SENS_TABLE","mi_status","cS","INDIVIDUAL"
)
.prefig_names <- intersect(.prefig_names, ls(envir=.RUN_ENV))
PRE_FIGURE_STATE <- mget(.prefig_names, envir=.RUN_ENV, inherits=FALSE)
saveRDS(PRE_FIGURE_STATE,
  file.path(CFG$outdir,"PRE_FIGURE_STATE_v27.rds"), compress="gzip")
message("Pre-figure state saved with ", length(PRE_FIGURE_STATE), " objects.")
rm(PRE_FIGURE_STATE, .prefig_names); invisible(gc())
# <<< INDIVIDUAL_BATTERY_V27_END <<<
```


# The evidence map and figures

```{r figures}
#| cache: false
# ---- safe figure-stage recovery ------------------------------------------------
# When this chunk is run on its own after a failed visual stage, restore only the
# compact objects saved immediately before figures. No microdata or models reload.
.figure_required <- c("CFG","CAT","COEF","DOM_ITEM","OSTER","LEADLAG","PI","HET_DEV","GRAD")
.figure_missing <- .figure_required[!vapply(
  .figure_required, exists, logical(1), envir=.RUN_ENV, inherits=FALSE)]
if (length(.figure_missing)) {
  .state_path <- file.path(CFG$outdir, "PRE_FIGURE_STATE_v27.rds")
  if (!file.exists(.state_path))
    stop("Figure inputs are missing and no pre-figure state exists: ", .state_path,
         "\nRun the pipeline through the individual_battery chunk once.")
  .state <- readRDS(.state_path)
  list2env(.state, envir=.RUN_ENV)
  rm(.state)
  .figure_missing <- .figure_required[!vapply(
    .figure_required, exists, logical(1), envir=.RUN_ENV, inherits=FALSE)]
  if (length(.figure_missing))
    stop("Pre-figure state is incomplete; missing: ", paste(.figure_missing, collapse=", "))
  message("Figure inputs restored from PRE_FIGURE_STATE_v27.rds")
}
rm(.figure_required, .figure_missing)
# ============================================================================
# SECTION 15: THE EVIDENCE MAP  (the "signature contribution", comment [2])
# ============================================================================
# Every predictor is assigned to exactly one of four types, from the criteria.
# The typology is the deliverable - not a shortlist of what "matters".

EM <- merge(
  dcast(COEF, code + label + domain + proximity ~ level,
        value.var=c("estimate","conf.low","conf.high","p_fdr","sig_fdr")),
  DOM_ITEM, by="code", all.x=TRUE)
EM <- merge(EM, OSTER[, .(code, robust_oster, robust_oster_between)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
EM <- merge(EM, LEADLAG[, .(code, order_ambiguous)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)

pi_w <- PI[level=="within",  .(code, imp_within=importance)]
pi_b <- PI[level=="between", .(code, imp_between=importance)]
EM <- merge(merge(EM, pi_w, by="code", all.x=TRUE), pi_b, by="code", all.x=TRUE)

het_var <- HET_DEV[level=="within",
                    .(het_range=max(estimate,na.rm=TRUE)-min(estimate,na.rm=TRUE)),
                    by=code]
het_test_w <- GRAD[level=="within",
                   .(code,
                     het_sig=heterogeneous_fdr,
                     het_difference=difference_high_low,
                     het_p_fdr=p_fdr_difference)]
het_test_b <- GRAD[level=="between",
                   .(code,
                     het_sig_between=heterogeneous_fdr,
                     het_difference_between=difference_high_low,
                     het_p_fdr_between=p_fdr_difference)]
het_var <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y,by="code",all=TRUE),
                  list(het_var, het_test_w, het_test_b))
EM <- merge(EM, het_var, by="code", all.x=TRUE)

# ---- classification rules ----
# The PRIMARY axis is the level at which the association holds, which is the
# question the dissertation exists to answer. Temporal ordering and context
# dependence are CAVEATS carried alongside that placement, not competing
# categories: a predictor whose ordering is ambiguous is still located at a
# level, and reporting it only as "order-ambiguous" would discard the finding.
# (An earlier version tested ordering first, which collapsed every predictor
# into that one bucket and destroyed the typology.)
EM[, has_within  := sig_fdr_within  == TRUE & !is.na(estimate_within)]
EM[, has_between := sig_fdr_between == TRUE & !is.na(estimate_between)]
EM[, has_ml_within  := !is.na(imp_within)  & imp_within  > 0]
EM[, has_ml_between := !is.na(imp_between) & imp_between > 0]
EM[, has_ml := has_ml_within]  # backward-compatible alias for older figures

EM[, within_grade := fcase(
  has_within & robust_oster == TRUE & has_ml_within, "Strong",
  has_within,                                           "Moderate",
  default=                                              "Not established")]
EM[, between_grade := fcase(
  has_between & robust_oster_between == TRUE & has_ml_between, "Strong",
  has_between,                                                  "Moderate",
  default=                                                     "Not established")]

# Location and evidential strength are separate dimensions. A predictor can be
# located within countries while carrying only moderate robustness, or be
# established at both levels with different grades.
EM[, evidence_type := fcase(
  has_within & has_between,  "Both levels",
  has_within,                "Dynamic (within-country)",
  has_between,               "Structural (between-country)",
  default=                   "Not established")]

# Caveats, appended to the placement rather than replacing it.
# Oster bounds and development-stratum heterogeneity are now computed at
# BOTH levels (Sections 3.7/3.8), reusing the same model fits -- no extra
# estimation, just no longer discarding the _b coefficient. Lead-lag
```
