# ordering (Section 3.9) remains within-only: the between component is, by
# construction, a single time-invariant country mean, so there is no
# temporal sequence within a country to lead or lag against. That is a
# structural property of the decomposition, not a gap left unexamined.
EM[, caveats := ""]
EM[order_ambiguous == TRUE, caveats := paste0(caveats, "order-ambiguous (within); ")]
EM[het_sig == TRUE,         caveats := paste0(caveats, "context-dependent (within); ")]
EM[!is.na(het_sig_between) & het_sig_between == TRUE,
   caveats := paste0(caveats, "context-dependent (between, ~56 countries/stratum -- lower power); ")]
EM[robust_oster == FALSE,   caveats := paste0(caveats, "sensitive to omitted confounding (within); ")]
EM[!is.na(robust_oster_between) & robust_oster_between == FALSE,
   caveats := paste0(caveats, "sensitive to omitted confounding (between); ")]

# All predictors are harmonised so higher values denote more favourable
# conditions. Significant negative coefficients are therefore explicitly
# marked as counter-directional rather than hidden inside a generic grade.
EM[, counterdirection_within :=
     has_within & !is.na(estimate_within) & estimate_within < 0]
EM[, counterdirection_between :=
     has_between & !is.na(estimate_between) & estimate_between < 0]
EM[counterdirection_within == TRUE,
   caveats := paste0(caveats, "counter-directional adjusted association (within); ")]
EM[counterdirection_between == TRUE,
   caveats := paste0(caveats, "counter-directional adjusted association (between); ")]
EM[!has_within & has_between,
   caveats := paste0(caveats, "temporal ordering not testable for a between-country association (no within-country time sequence to compare); ")]
EM[, caveats := trimws(sub("; $", "", caveats))]

## ---- informative nulls: equivalence-style precision classification ----
# For within-level candidates that do not survive FDR, distinguish CIs
# narrow enough to EXCLUDE effects as large as the smallest confirmed one
# (precise null) from CIs still compatible with such effects (inconclusive).
# SESOI = smallest |estimate| among FDR-surviving within effects.
SESOI <- COEF[level=="within" & sig_fdr==TRUE, min(abs(estimate))]
NULLCLS <- COEF[level=="within" & sig_fdr==FALSE,
                .(code, null_class = fifelse(conf.low > -SESOI & conf.high < SESOI,
                                             "precise null", "inconclusive"))]
EM <- merge(EM, NULLCLS, by="code", all.x=TRUE)
EM[evidence_type=="Not established" & !is.na(null_class),
   evidence_type := paste0("Not established (", null_class, ")")]

EM[, evidence_type_full := fifelse(caveats == "", evidence_type,
                                   paste0(evidence_type, " (", caveats, ")"))]

setorder(EM, -imp_between, -imp_within)
# >>> THESIS Table 3 candidate ("Graded Evidence for Within-Country Associations Among 29 Catalogue Predictors") -- MEDIUM-HIGH confidence. See also T18a below, which may be the closer match; verify against docx. <<<
fwrite(EM, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T18_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv"))

# ---- publication-facing result tables ----
# A compact main-text table contains every predictor established at either
# level. The master appendix register retains all diagnostics for auditability.
MAIN_RES <- EM[within_grade != "Not established" |
               between_grade != "Not established",
  .(code, label, domain, proximity,
    within_beta=estimate_within,
    within_ci_low=conf.low_within,
    within_ci_high=conf.high_within,
    within_grade,
    between_beta=estimate_between,
    between_ci_low=conf.low_between,
    between_ci_high=conf.high_between,
    between_grade,
    counterdirection_within,
    counterdirection_between,
    evidence_type,
    caveats)]
MAIN_RES[, `:=`(.ord_within = abs(within_beta),
                  .ord_between = abs(between_beta))]
setorderv(MAIN_RES,
          c("domain", ".ord_within", ".ord_between"),
          c(1L, -1L, -1L),
          na.last = TRUE)
MAIN_RES[, c(".ord_within", ".ord_between") := NULL]
# >>> THESIS Table 3 candidate (alternative to T18 above) -- MEDIUM-HIGH confidence <<<
fwrite(MAIN_RES, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T18a_MAIN_RESULTS.csv"))

FULL_REGISTER <- EM[, .(
  code, label, domain, proximity,
  estimate_within, conf.low_within, conf.high_within,
  p_fdr_within, sig_fdr_within, within_grade,
  estimate_between, conf.low_between, conf.high_between,
  p_fdr_between, sig_fdr_between, between_grade,
  counterdirection_within, counterdirection_between,
  unique_r2_w, unique_r2_b,
  robust_oster, robust_oster_between,
  imp_within, imp_between,
  order_ambiguous,
  het_difference, het_p_fdr, het_sig,
  het_difference_between, het_p_fdr_between, het_sig_between,
  evidence_type, null_class, caveats)]
setorder(FULL_REGISTER, domain, label)
fwrite(FULL_REGISTER,
       # >>> THESIS Table 8 ("The Evidence Map in Summary") -- MEDIUM-HIGH confidence <<<
       file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T18b_FULL_EVIDENCE_REGISTER.csv"))

TYPO <- EM[, .N, by=evidence_type][order(-N)]
n_amb_em <- EM[order_ambiguous == TRUE, .N]
n_het_em <- EM[het_sig == TRUE, .N]

TYPOLOGY_S <- sprintf(
  "Applying the classification criteria assigns each of the %d catalogue predictors to a single evidence location: %s. Alongside that placement, %d predictor(s) carry a temporal-ordering caveat and %d show a formally tested high-versus-low-development difference surviving false-discovery-rate correction. Evidential strength is reported separately at the within- and between-country levels, preventing location from being conflated with robustness.",
  nrow(EM),
  paste(sprintf("%d %s", TYPO$N, tolower(TYPO$evidence_type)), collapse="; "),
  n_amb_em, n_het_em)

# Degeneracy check: if one bucket holds nearly everything the criteria are not
# discriminating, and the thesis says that null pattern must be reported rather
# than absorbed into selective interpretation.
if (TYPO[1, N] / nrow(EM) > 0.80)
  warning(sprintf("%.0f%% of predictors fall in a single evidence type ('%s'). ",
                  100*TYPO[1,N]/nrow(EM), TYPO[1, evidence_type]),
          "Check the criteria are discriminating before reporting the typology.")

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 16: FIGURES
# ============================================================================
# Palette: a diverging pair chosen for the level contrast (within vs between),
# on a warm neutral ground. Deliberately NOT viridis or RdBu defaults - the two
# levels are the argument, so they get the two strongest hues and everything
# else is muted grey. Serif titles to match a dissertation body text.

PAL <- list(
  within  = "#1B6C7A",   # deep teal   - change inside countries
  between = "#B5502E",   # burnt sienna - differences across countries
  neutral = "#6B665F",
  ground  = "#FAF8F4",
  rule    = "#D8D2C8",
  ink     = "#22201D")

theme_thesis <- function(base=11) {
  theme_minimal(base_size=base, base_family="serif") +
  theme(
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill=PAL$ground, colour=NA),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill=PAL$ground, colour=NA),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.3),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    axis.text         = element_text(colour=PAL$ink, size=base-1),
    axis.title        = element_text(colour=PAL$ink, size=base-1),
    plot.title        = element_text(face="bold", size=base+3, colour=PAL$ink,
                                     margin=margin(b=4)),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size=base-1, colour=PAL$neutral,
                                     margin=margin(b=10), lineheight=1.15),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size=base-3, colour=PAL$neutral, hjust=0,
                                     margin=margin(t=10), lineheight=1.15),
    strip.text        = element_text(face="bold", colour=PAL$ink, size=base-1),
    legend.position   = "top",
    legend.title      = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.margin       = margin(14,16,12,14))
}
sv <- function(p, name, w=9, h=7)
  ggsave(file.path(CFG$outdir,"fig",name), p, width=w, height=h, dpi=320, bg=PAL$ground)





# >>> VISUAL_SYSTEM_V28_START >>>
# ============================================================================
# VISUAL SYSTEM V28: ACADEMIC, ACCESSIBLE, SIMPLE AND CONSISTENT
# ============================================================================
# This block overrides the common palette/theme/save helper before any figure is
# drawn. Every later figure inherits the same typography, spacing, colour logic
# and export standard. Key result tables are also exported as styled HTML files.

PAL <- list(
  within     = "#0B6E75",   # teal: change within countries
  between    = "#C45D3A",   # terracotta: differences between countries
  individual = "#6656A3",   # violet: differences between respondents
  neutral    = "#73777A",
  ground     = "#FCFBF8",
  rule       = "#D7D4CF",
  ink        = "#20262B",
  positive   = "#2E7D32",
  negative   = "#A33A3A"
)

FIG_DIR  <- file.path(CFG$outdir, "fig")
HTML_DIR <- file.path(CFG$outdir, "tab_html")
dir.create(FIG_DIR,  recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
dir.create(HTML_DIR, recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)

theme_thesis <- function(base=11) {
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=base, base_family="sans") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.background      = ggplot2::element_rect(fill=PAL$ground, colour=NA),
      panel.background     = ggplot2::element_rect(fill=PAL$ground, colour=NA),
      plot.title.position  = "plot",
      plot.caption.position= "plot",
      plot.title           = ggplot2::element_text(face="bold", size=base*1.38,
                                                   colour=PAL$ink, margin=ggplot2::margin(b=7)),
      plot.subtitle        = ggplot2::element_text(size=base*.96, colour="#4B5155",
                                                   lineheight=1.10, margin=ggplot2::margin(b=10)),
      plot.caption         = ggplot2::element_text(size=base*.73, colour="#666A6D",
                                                   lineheight=1.08, hjust=0,
                                                   margin=ggplot2::margin(t=10)),
      axis.title           = ggplot2::element_text(face="bold", colour=PAL$ink),
      axis.text            = ggplot2::element_text(colour=PAL$ink),
      strip.text           = ggplot2::element_text(face="bold", colour=PAL$ink),
      panel.grid.minor     = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major     = ggplot2::element_line(colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.35),
      legend.position      = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      legend.title         = ggplot2::element_text(face="bold"),
      legend.key           = ggplot2::element_rect(fill=PAL$ground, colour=NA),
      plot.margin          = ggplot2::margin(14, 18, 12, 14)
    )
}

ggplot2::theme_set(theme_thesis())

sv <- function(p, name, w=9, h=7, dpi=360) {
  png_name <- if (grepl("\\.png$", name, ignore.case=TRUE)) name else paste0(name, ".png")
  png_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, png_name)
  ggplot2::ggsave(png_path, p, width=w, height=h, dpi=dpi,
                  bg=PAL$ground, limitsize=FALSE)

  # Vector PDF is attempted for thesis insertion; a PDF-device problem must not
  # interrupt the run because the high-resolution PNG is already complete.
  pdf_path <- sub("\\.png$", ".pdf", png_path, ignore.case=TRUE)
  try(
    ggplot2::ggsave(pdf_path, p, width=w, height=h,
                    device=grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg=PAL$ground,
                    limitsize=FALSE),
    silent=TRUE
  )
  invisible(png_path)
}

fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, digits=3) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f  [%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"), est, lo, hi)
}

save_gt_clean <- function(x, filename, title, subtitle=NULL, note=NULL,
                          percent_cols=character(), integer_cols=character(),
                          decimals=3) {
  if (!requireNamespace("gt", quietly=TRUE) || is.null(x) || !nrow(x)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  d <- as.data.frame(x)
  num <- names(d)[vapply(d, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  dec <- setdiff(num, union(percent_cols, integer_cols))

  tab <- gt::gt(d) |>
    gt::tab_header(title=gt::md(paste0("**", title, "**")), subtitle=subtitle) |>
    gt::opt_row_striping() |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.font.names=c("Arial", "Helvetica", "sans-serif"),
      table.font.size=gt::px(13),
      heading.title.font.size=gt::px(20),
      heading.subtitle.font.size=gt::px(13),
      heading.align="left",
      table.background.color=PAL$ground,
      column_labels.background.color="#EEEAE4",
      column_labels.font.weight="bold",
      row.striping.background_color="#F5F2ED",
      data_row.padding=gt::px(6),
      table.border.top.color=PAL$ink,
      table.border.top.width=gt::px(2),
      table.border.bottom.color=PAL$ink,
      table.border.bottom.width=gt::px(1)
    )
  if (length(dec)) tab <- gt::fmt_number(tab, columns=tidyselect::all_of(dec), decimals=decimals)
  if (length(percent_cols)) tab <- gt::fmt_percent(tab, columns=tidyselect::all_of(percent_cols), decimals=1)
  if (length(integer_cols)) tab <- gt::fmt_integer(tab, columns=tidyselect::all_of(integer_cols), use_seps=TRUE)
  if (!is.null(note) && nzchar(note)) tab <- gt::tab_source_note(tab, gt::md(note))
  gt::gtsave(tab, file.path(HTML_DIR, filename))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# ---- Clean, thesis-ready summary tables --------------------------------------
tryCatch({
  if (exists("EM") && nrow(EM)) {
    E <- data.table::copy(EM)
    E[, within_result := fmt_ci(estimate_within, conf.low_within, conf.high_within)]
    E[, between_result := fmt_ci(estimate_between, conf.low_between, conf.high_between)]
    keep <- intersect(c("domain","label","within_result","within_grade",
                        "between_result","between_grade","evidence_type","caveats"), names(E))
    E <- E[, ..keep]
    E <- E[order(domain, label)]
    save_gt_clean(E, "T18_evidence_map_readable.html",
      "Evidence map: where each predictor is established",
      "Within-country change and between-country differences are displayed as distinct estimands.",
      "Coefficients are adjusted associations. Grades combine multiplicity control, robustness and predictive evidence; caveats remain visible rather than being hidden.")
  }
}, error=function(e) message("Readable evidence table skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)))

tryCatch({
  if (!is.null(INDIVIDUAL)) {
    M <- data.table::copy(INDIVIDUAL$model_comparison)
    if (nrow(M)) {
      M[, `:=`(`Within R² (%)`=100*within_r2,
               `Incremental R² (pp)`=100*incremental_within_r2)]
      M <- M[, .(
        Model=model, Question=question, Respondents=n, Countries=n_countries,
        `Country-years`=n_country_years, `Within R² (%)`, `Incremental R² (pp)`
      )]
      save_gt_clean(M, "T28_individual_model_comparison_readable.html",
        "What the respondent layer adds",
        "Nested models use the same respondents and country-year fixed effects.",
        "R² is computed within country-year. It measures explanatory fit, not causal importance.",
        integer_cols=intersect(c("Respondents","Countries","Country-years"), names(M)), decimals=2)
    }

    C <- data.table::copy(INDIVIDUAL$coefficients)
    if (nrow(C)) {
      C <- C[!grepl("missing", term, ignore.case=TRUE)]
      C[, `95% CI` := fmt_ci(estimate, conf.low, conf.high)]
      C[, `FDR result` := data.table::fifelse(sig_fdr, "Established", "Not established")]
      C <- C[, intersect(c("label","95% CI","p_fdr","FDR result"), names(C)), with=FALSE]
      save_gt_clean(C, "T29_individual_coefficients_readable.html",
        "Respondent-level structural associations",
        "Comparisons are between people interviewed in the same country and year.",
        "Country-clustered confidence intervals; Benjamini-Hochberg correction is applied within the respondent-level family.")
    }

    H <- data.table::copy(INDIVIDUAL$heterogeneity_tests)
    if (nrow(H)) {
      H[, conclusion := data.table::fifelse(heterogeneous_fdr,
        "Income gradient differs across groups", "No FDR-surviving difference")]
      H <- H[, intersect(c("moderator","statistic","p.value","p_fdr","conclusion"), names(H)), with=FALSE]
      save_gt_clean(H, "T32_individual_heterogeneity_readable.html",
        "Where the individual income gradient differs",
        "Formal omnibus interaction tests across the pre-specified subgroup battery.",
        "The FDR column controls multiplicity across moderator families. Non-significance is not interpreted as equality without regard to precision.")
    }
  }
}, error=function(e) message("Readable individual tables skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)))
# <<< VISUAL_SYSTEM_V28_END <<<


# >>> INDIVIDUAL_BATTERY_FIGURES_V27_START >>>
# ============================================================================
# RESPONDENT-LAYER FIGURES: THREE FIGURES, ONE COHERENT STORY
# ============================================================================
# These figures are generated from compact CSV-ready tables. They never need the
# respondent microdata or fitted models, so figure recovery is now cheap.

if (!is.null(INDIVIDUAL)) {
  ## ---- F32: individual structural associations ------------------------------
  tryCatch({
    IC <- copy(INDIVIDUAL$coefficients)
    IC <- IC[!grepl("missing", term, ignore.case=TRUE)]
    IC <- IC[!grepl("children_missing", term, fixed=TRUE)]
    stopifnot(nrow(IC) > 0)
    IC[, domain := fcase(
      grepl("income", term), "Resources",
      grepl("employment", term), "Employment",
      grepl("age|sex|educ|urban|marital|children", term), "Demographic composition",
      default="Other")]
    IC[, label := factor(label, levels=IC[order(estimate), label])]
    f32 <- ggplot(IC, aes(estimate, label, colour=domain)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept=0, colour=PAL$ink, linewidth=.4) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin=conf.low, xmax=conf.high), height=0, linewidth=.75) +
      geom_point(data=IC[sig_fdr==TRUE], aes(fill=domain), shape=21, size=2.8, stroke=.55) +
      geom_point(data=IC[sig_fdr==FALSE], fill="white", shape=21, size=2.6, stroke=.65) +
      scale_fill_manual(values=c(Resources=PAL$within, Employment=PAL$between,
                                 `Demographic composition`=PAL$neutral, Other=PAL$ink), guide="none") +
      scale_colour_manual(values=c(Resources=PAL$within, Employment=PAL$between,
                                   `Demographic composition`=PAL$neutral, Other=PAL$ink),
                          name=NULL) +
      labs(
        title="Individual inequality remains after holding national context fixed",
        subtitle="Associations among respondents interviewed in the same country and year, from a country-year fixed-effects model.\nEvery point therefore compares people exposed to the same national conditions and survey wave; filled outlines survive\nBenjamini-Hochberg correction within the respondent-level family.",
        x="Difference in Cantril ladder points", y=NULL,
        caption="Country-clustered 95% confidence intervals. Coefficients are adjusted for the other displayed structural characteristics.\nThey describe cross-sectional differences between respondents, not within-person change and not causal effects.") +
      theme_thesis() +
      theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=8.1), panel.grid.major.y=element_blank(),
            legend.position="top")
    sv(f32, "F32_individual_structural_associations.png", 11, 8.8)
  }, error=function(e) message("F32 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)))

  ## ---- F33: full pre-specified heterogeneity battery ------------------------
  tryCatch({
    HS <- copy(INDIVIDUAL$group_slopes)
    stopifnot(nrow(HS) > 0)
    HS[, moderator_lab := paste0(moderator,
      fifelse(heterogeneous_fdr==TRUE, "  • heterogeneous after FDR", ""))]
    HS[, group := factor(group, levels=rev(unique(group)))]
    f33 <- ggplot(HS, aes(estimate, group,
                          colour=heterogeneous_fdr, alpha=heterogeneous_fdr)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept=0, colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.5) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin=conf.low, xmax=conf.high), height=.08, linewidth=.7) +
      geom_point(size=2.5) +
      facet_wrap(~moderator_lab, scales="free_y", ncol=2) +
      scale_colour_manual(values=c(`TRUE`=PAL$between, `FALSE`=PAL$within),
                          labels=c(`TRUE`="Omnibus heterogeneity survives FDR",
                                   `FALSE`="No FDR-surviving heterogeneity"), name=NULL) +
      scale_alpha_manual(values=c(`TRUE`=1, `FALSE`=.72), guide="none") +
      labs(
        title="The individual income gradient is widespread, but not automatically universal",
        subtitle="Group-specific slopes for a one-SD difference in household-income position among contemporaneous compatriots.\nEach panel comes from one full interaction model with the same controls and country-year fixed effects; the coloured\nclassification is the formal omnibus interaction test after correction across the pre-specified moderator battery.",
        x="Cantril points per SD of relative household income", y=NULL,
        caption="Country-clustered 95% confidence intervals. Groups below the pre-stated respondent, country and country-year support\nthresholds are excluded and documented in T34. Heterogeneity is descriptive association heterogeneity, not treatment-effect heterogeneity.") +
      theme_thesis(base=10.5) +
      theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=7.7), strip.text=element_text(size=9, face="bold"),
            panel.grid.major.y=element_blank(), legend.position="top")
    # >>> THESIS Figure 16 ("The Relative-Income Gradient Across 27 Pre-Specified Subgroups") -- HIGH confidence <<<
sv(f33, "F33_individual_income_heterogeneity.png", 12.5, 12)
  }, error=function(e) message("F33 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)))

  ## ---- F34: incremental respondent-level explanatory power -----------------
  tryCatch({
    MC <- copy(INDIVIDUAL$model_comparison)
    stopifnot(nrow(MC) >= 3)
    MC[, model_lab := fcase(
      model=="Country-year context only", "Context only",
      model=="Demographic composition", "Demographic\ncomposition",
      model=="Full structural respondent model", "Full respondent\nstructure",
      model=="Non-linear income sensitivity", "Non-linear income\nsensitivity",
      default=model)]
    MC[, model_lab := factor(model_lab, levels=rev(model_lab))]
    MC[, pct := 100*within_r2]
    MC[, gain := pct - pct[1]]
    f34 <- ggplot(MC, aes(model_lab, pct, fill=model_lab)) +
      geom_col(width=.62) +
      geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)), hjust=-.18,
                family="serif", fontface="bold", size=4, colour=PAL$ink) +
      coord_flip(clip="off") +
      scale_fill_manual(values=c("#8B6F47", PAL$between, PAL$within, PAL$neutral), guide="none") +
      scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,.20)), labels=function(x) paste0(x,"%")) +
      labs(
        title="How much of the difference between people can the survey actually explain?",
        subtitle="Within-country-year R-squared from nested models estimated on the same respondents. Country-year fixed effects first\nremove all shared national context; demographics then measure composition, and income plus employment add the\nstructural respondent layer. The remaining variance is not evidence that unmeasured biography or personality do not matter.",
        x=NULL, y="Within-country-year R-squared",
        caption=sprintf("Common analytical sample: N = %s respondents across %d countries and %d country-years. The final bar tests\na quadratic relative-income term; it is a functional-form sensitivity, not a separate substantive model.",
          format(INDIVIDUAL$n, big.mark=","), INDIVIDUAL$n_countries, INDIVIDUAL$n_country_years)) +
      theme_thesis() +
      theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=9.5, face="bold", lineheight=.95),
            panel.grid.major.y=element_blank())
    # >>> DRAFT superseded by F42_individual_incremental_r2_clean.png (see "CANDIDATE MAIN-TEXT FIGURES" section, Figure C) = THESIS Figure 12. Kept here as an intermediate diagnostic. <<<
sv(f34, "F34_individual_incremental_r2.png", 10.5, 6.6)
  }, error=function(e) message("F34 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)))
}

## ---- FIG 1: THE EVIDENCE MAP HEATMAP (signature figure) ----
HM <- melt(EM[, .(label,
                  `Within-country\ncoefficient`  = estimate_within,
                  `Between-country\ncoefficient` = estimate_between,
                  `Unique R² \nwithin`           = unique_r2_w,

                  `ML importance\nwithin`        = imp_within,
                  `ML importance\nbetween`       = imp_between)],
           id.vars="label", variable.name="criterion", value.name="v")
HM[, z := scale(v)[,1], by=criterion]     # comparable across differing units

HM[, label := factor(label, levels=EM[order(imp_between), label])]

f1 <- ggplot(HM, aes(criterion, label, fill=z)) +
  geom_tile(colour=PAL$ground, linewidth=1.1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low=PAL$between, mid=PAL$ground, high=PAL$within,

  facet_grid(evidence_type ~ ., scales="free_y", space="free_y", switch="y") +

       x=NULL, y=NULL,
       caption=sprintf("Gallup World Poll, %d countries, %d contributing to within-country estimates. CRE-Mundlak specification.\nSignificance assessed after Benjamini-Hochberg correction within declared families.",
                       Q1$n_countries_total, Q1$n_countries_within)) +
  theme_thesis() +
  theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=8.5), legend.position="right",

## ---- FIG 6 (thesis Figure 6): established within-country associations at both levels ----
# Added during the reproducibility audit: previously no code produced this
# specific figure. F04 above shows all 29 predictors across both levels; this
# is a distinct, filtered view -- only the 14 predictors established
# within-country, read at both national levels, matching Figure 6's own note:
# "Rows are selected solely because the within-country coefficient survives
# BH-FDR q < .05 ... In the between-country panel, filled markers denote the
# five coefficients that also survive BH-FDR there; open markers denote a
# non-established between-country counterpart."
f6 <- tryCatch({
  established14 <- EM[within_grade %in% c("Strong", "Moderate"), code]
  stopifnot(length(established14) == 14L)

  C6 <- COEF[code %in% established14]
  stopifnot(nrow(C6) == 28L)  # 14 predictors x 2 levels

  ord6 <- C6[level == "within"][order(abs(estimate))]
  C6[, label := factor(label, levels = ord6$label)]
  C6[, level_lab := factor(level, levels = c("within", "between"),
                            labels = c("Within-country", "Between-country"))]
  # Within panel is established by construction (always filled); between
  # panel distinguishes established (filled) from not (open) via sig_fdr.
  C6[, established_here := fifelse(level == "within", TRUE, sig_fdr)]

  f6_plot <- ggplot(C6, aes(estimate, label, colour = level)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = .45) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0, linewidth = .55) +
    geom_point(data = C6[established_here == TRUE], shape = 21, size = 2.8,
               stroke = .6, aes(fill = level)) +
    geom_point(data = C6[established_here == FALSE], shape = 21, size = 2.6,
               stroke = .7, fill = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~level_lab, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(within = PAL$within, between = PAL$between), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(within = PAL$within, between = PAL$between), guide = "none") +
    labs(title = "Established Within-Country Associations Read at Both National Levels",
         subtitle = paste(strwrap(
           "Rows are the 14 predictors established within countries, by construction. In the between-country panel, filled markers survive BH-FDR there too; open markers do not.",
           width = 120), collapse = "\n"),
         x = "Coefficient (Cantril ladder points)", y = NULL,
         caption = "Estimates are from the final 29-predictor CRE-Mundlak model.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.4),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
  # >>> THESIS Figure 6 ("Established Within-Country Associations Read at Both National Levels") -- HIGH confidence, structurally matches the docx note (14 rows, filled/open by BH-FDR) <<<
  sv(f6_plot, "F44_established_within_both_levels.png", 10.5, 7.5)

VP[, model := factor(model, c("r2_linear","r2_enet","r2_xgb"),
                     c("Linear CRE","Elastic net","Gradient boosting"))]
VP[, design := factor(design, c("random","temporal","country","development"),

  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::number_format(accuracy=.01)) +
  labs(title="Relaxing the functional form recovers little additional signal",
       subtitle=sprintf("Out-of-sample R² on identical held-out observations. The boosted model's gain over the linear specification\non the country holdout is %.3f, bounding the risk that the CRE coefficients are artefacts of an imposed parametric form.",
                        FUNCFORM$gain_country),
       x=NULL, y="Out-of-sample R²",
       caption="Four designs reported together. Presenting only the random split would overstate generalisation, since respondents\nfrom the same country-year share identical country-level predictors and fall on both sides of that split.") +
  theme_thesis()

       x=NULL, y="Within-country coefficient",
       caption="A test of the needs-hierarchy proposition (Tay & Diener, 2011). Heterogeneity counts as confirmatory only where a\nstratum-specific association survives false-discovery-rate correction.") +

## ---- FIG 2b: THE LEVEL CONTRAST, REDESIGNED FOR LEGIBILITY ----
# F02 colours by thematic domain (eight hues) while the ARGUMENT is the
# quadrant, and labels all 30 predictors at 2.7pt, which ggrepel stacks into
# an unreadable pile. This version: two colours (the argument), corner zone
# labels so the 2x2 reads without the caption, selective labelling of the
# twelve largest plus any Robust/Specification-dependent predictor, and fixed
# coordinates so the diagonal means something geometrically. F02 is kept so
# both can be compared.
F02B <- tryCatch({
  CD <- EM[!is.na(estimate_within) & !is.na(estimate_between)]
  stopifnot(nrow(CD) > 0)
  CD[, quadrant := fifelse(abs(estimate_within) >= abs(estimate_between),
                            "Dynamic: moves with change inside countries",
                            "Structural: separates countries, not their change")]
  CD[, mag := pmax(abs(estimate_within), abs(estimate_between))]
  CD[, lab_show := fifelse(rank(-mag) <= 12 |
                            evidence_type %chin% c("Robust","Specification-dependent"),
                            label, NA_character_)]
  lim <- max(abs(c(CD$estimate_within, CD$estimate_between)), na.rm=TRUE) * 1.18

  f2b <- ggplot(CD, aes(estimate_between, estimate_within)) +
    geom_abline(slope=1,  intercept=0, linetype="22", colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.7) +
    geom_abline(slope=-1, intercept=0, linetype="22", colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept=0, colour=PAL$ink, linewidth=.35) +
    geom_vline(xintercept=0, colour=PAL$ink, linewidth=.35) +
    annotate("text", x=lim*.93, y=lim*.93, label="Both levels", hjust=1, vjust=1,
             size=3.1, family="serif", colour=PAL$neutral, fontface="italic") +
    annotate("text", x=lim*.93, y=-lim*.93, label="Between only\n(structural gradient)",
             hjust=1, vjust=0, size=3.1, family="serif", colour=PAL$between,
             fontface="italic", lineheight=.95) +
    annotate("text", x=-lim*.93, y=lim*.93, label="Within only\n(policy lever)",
             hjust=0, vjust=1, size=3.1, family="serif", colour=PAL$within,
             fontface="italic", lineheight=.95) +
    geom_point(aes(colour=quadrant, size=unique_r2_w), alpha=.9) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label=lab_show), size=3.05, family="serif",
                             colour=PAL$ink, na.rm=TRUE, seed=1, max.overlaps=Inf,
                             box.padding=.55, point.padding=.35,
                             min.segment.length=.15, segment.colour=PAL$rule,
                             segment.size=.35, force=2.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=c(`Dynamic: moves with change inside countries`=PAL$within,
                                  `Structural: separates countries, not their change`=PAL$between)) +
    scale_size_continuous(range=c(2.2, 8.5), guide="none") +
    coord_fixed(xlim=c(-lim, lim), ylim=c(-lim, lim), clip="off") +
    labs(title="Where a condition matters is not where it appears to matter",
         subtitle="Each point is one condition of life. The horizontal axis is its association with life evaluation ACROSS countries;\nthe vertical axis is its association WITH CHANGE INSIDE a country. Points far from the diagonal are the argument:\ntheir apparent importance depends entirely on which level is read. Only the twelve largest are labelled.",
         x="Between-country coefficient  ->  differences across nations",
         y="Within-country coefficient  ->  change inside a nation", colour=NULL,
         caption="Point size is unique within-country explained variance. Dashed diagonals mark equal magnitude at both levels.\nA pooled specification that does not separate these axes reports a single number somewhere between them, and\nattributes a cross-national regularity to within-country dynamics.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position="top", legend.text=element_text(size=9),
          panel.grid.minor=element_blank())
  # >>> THESIS Figure 8 ("Within- and Between-Country Coefficients for the Full National Catalogue") -- HIGH confidence. Supersedes draft F02 above. <<<
sv(f2b, "F02b_level_contrast_clean.png", 10.5, 10); TRUE
}, error=function(e){ message("F02b skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })


## ---- FIG 2c: THE LEVEL CONTRAST, FACETED BY DEVELOPMENT STRATUM ----
# F02b's within/between contrast uses ONE global model: there is one coefficient
# per predictor, not one per stratum. Segmenting requires HET_DEV, which
# re-estimates the specification separately within each development stratum.
# POWER WARNING: each stratum pools ~56 countries, so panel-specific
# coefficients are considerably less precise than the global ones -- especially
# the between-country ones, which are identified from the variation across
# countries within the stratum. The figure is descriptive of heterogeneity,
# not a basis for comparing magnitudes across panels.
F02C <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("HET_DEV"), nrow(HET_DEV) > 0)
  H <- copy(HET_DEV)

  # v16 adds the 'level' column to HET_DEV (within and between); earlier
  # versions only estimated within. Both cases are handled here.
  if (!"level" %in% names(H)) H[, level := "within"]

  HW <- dcast(H[level %chin% c("within","between")],
              stratum + code ~ level, value.var = "estimate")
  if (!"between" %in% names(HW)) {
    # No between-country term per stratum: the stratum's within-country coefficient is plotted
    # against the GLOBAL between-country coefficient, which is constant across panels. This is stated explicitly.
    HW <- merge(HW, EM[, .(code, between = estimate_between)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
    sub_note <- "Vertical axis: within-country coefficient re-estimated inside each development stratum.\nHorizontal axis: the global between-country coefficient, identical across panels (not re-estimated by stratum)."
  } else {
    sub_note <- "Both coefficients re-estimated separately inside each development stratum. Between-country estimates rest on\nroughly 56 countries per panel and are correspondingly less precise than the pooled estimates of the previous figure."
  }
  setnames(HW, "within", "within_est", skip_absent=TRUE)
  HW <- HW[!is.na(within_est) & !is.na(between)]
  stopifnot(nrow(HW) > 0)

  HW <- merge(HW, CAT[, .(code, label)], by="code", all.x=TRUE)
  HW[code=="ln_gdp", label := "GDP per capita (log)"]
  sig_map <- unique(H[level=="within", .(stratum, code, sig_fdr)])
  HW <- merge(HW, sig_map, by=c("stratum","code"), all.x=TRUE)
  HW[is.na(sig_fdr), sig_fdr := FALSE]

  HW[, stratum := factor(stratum, levels=c("Low income","Middle income","High income"))]
  HW[, quadrant := fifelse(abs(within_est) >= abs(between),
                            "Dynamic: larger within-country",
                            "Structural: larger between-country")]
  # Label only what is legible: the 5 largest per panel, and only if they survive FDR.
  HW[, mag := pmax(abs(within_est), abs(between))]
  HW[, lab_show := fifelse(sig_fdr == TRUE & rank(-mag) <= 5, label, NA_character_), by=stratum]
  liml <- max(abs(c(HW$within_est, HW$between)), na.rm=TRUE) * 1.15

  f2c <- ggplot(HW, aes(between, within_est)) +
    geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="22", colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept=0, colour=PAL$ink, linewidth=.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept=0, colour=PAL$ink, linewidth=.3) +
    geom_point(aes(colour=quadrant, alpha=sig_fdr), size=2.6) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label=lab_show), size=2.7, family="serif",
                             colour=PAL$ink, na.rm=TRUE, seed=1, max.overlaps=Inf,
                             box.padding=.45, min.segment.length=.15,
                             segment.colour=PAL$rule, segment.size=.3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=c(`Dynamic: larger within-country`=PAL$within,
                                  `Structural: larger between-country`=PAL$between)) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values=c(`TRUE`=.95, `FALSE`=.28),
                       labels=c(`TRUE`="Survives FDR", `FALSE`="Does not survive FDR")) +
    facet_wrap(~ stratum, nrow=1) +
    coord_fixed(xlim=c(-liml, liml), ylim=c(-liml, liml)) +
    labs(title="The same conditions, read at three levels of development",
         subtitle=sub_note,
         x="Between-country coefficient", y="Within-country coefficient",
         colour=NULL, alpha=NULL,
         caption="Only the five largest FDR-surviving predictors are labelled per panel. Faded points do not survive false-discovery-rate\ncorrection within their stratum. Panels are not directly comparable in magnitude: each rests on a different subsample of\ncountries, and the within-country estimates carry the power of roughly a third of the panel each.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position="top", legend.box="vertical", legend.spacing.y=unit(1,"pt"),
          strip.text=element_text(face="bold", size=10),
          panel.grid.minor=element_blank())
  sv(f2c, "F02c_level_contrast_by_development.png", 13, 6); TRUE
}, error=function(e){ message("F02c skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })


# ============================================================================
# SECTION 16b: DOCUMENTATION TABLES  (design made auditable)
# ============================================================================
# These tables document decisions already taken elsewhere in the pipeline. They
# estimate nothing, so they are cheap and cannot fail the run; their purpose is
# to let a reader audit the design without reconstructing it from prose.

T22 <- tryCatch({
  n_ctrl <- length(intersect(CONTROLS, names(ANA)))
  tab <- data.table(
    level = c("Level 3 - country","Level 2 - country-year",
              "Level 1 - respondent (composition)",
              "Level 1 - respondent (relative position)","Time"),
    unit_of_variation = c(
      "Stable differences between the sampled countries",
      "Year-to-year movement within a country across waves",
      "Differences between respondents surveyed in the same country-year",
      "A respondent's income position relative to peers in the same country-year",
      "Shocks common to all countries in a given calendar year"),
    how_entered = c(
      sprintf("%d between-country terms (_b: country mean, centred and scaled on the distribution of country means) + random intercept (1|iso3)", length(B_VARS)),
      sprintf("%d within-country terms (_w: country-year deviation from that country's own mean, scaled by pooled within SD) + random intercept (1|cy)", length(W_VARS)),
      sprintf("%d sociodemographic controls entered at respondent level (robustness specification)", n_ctrl),
      "ln_income_h_p: log household income minus the weighted mean of the respondent's reference group",
      "Year fixed effects (yearf)"),
    what_it_supports = c(
      "Cross-national gradients: which conditions distinguish countries reporting higher life evaluation",
      "Within-country association: whether life evaluation moves as a country changes. The primary estimand",
      "Compositional robustness: whether associations survive adjustment for who is surveyed",
      "Cross-sectional relative-position association at a single moment",
      "Absorbs global shocks and wave-specific fielding changes"),
    what_it_cannot_support = c(
      "Temporal ordering: the between component is one time-invariant value per country, so there is no sequence to lead or lag",
      "Causality: time-varying confounding is quantified by Oster bounds, not removed",
      "Individual causal mechanisms: controls adjust for composition, they do not identify mechanisms",
      "Within-person change: the survey is a repeated cross-section, so no respondent is observed twice",
      "Country-specific time trends, which are not modelled separately"),
    reported_in = c("T03, T09, F02b","T03, T09, T11, F02b","T03c","T20, T21, T27, F12","T03"))
  # >>> THESIS Table 1 ("Levels of Analysis: What Each Level Enters As...") -- HIGH confidence (name match) <<<
  fwrite(tab, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T22_analysis_levels.csv")); tab
}, error=function(e){ message("T22 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

T23 <- tryCatch({
  tab <- data.table(
    step = 1:9,
    stage = c("Raw extract (parquet)","Catalogue assembled on capability-theoretic grounds",
              "High-proximity items excluded","Range and direction cleaning",
              "Coverage and within-variation screening","Collapse to country-year, weighted",
              "Mundlak decomposition","Missingness handling","Analytical sample"),
    what_happens = c(
      "All respondent rows read for catalogue columns plus weights and sociodemographics",
      "Items mapped to theoretical domains, each with codebook-verified valid range and coding direction",
      "Items that restate the outcome rather than a domain-specific condition are removed, blocked by assertion at four points",
      "Out-of-range values set to missing; reverse-coded items flipped so higher always means more favourable",
      "Items must clear minimum country-years, minimum countries and minimum within-country SD",
      "Predictors averaged to country-year using the individual sampling weight; the outcome stays at respondent level",
      "Each predictor split into a between-country and a within-country component, entered as separate terms",
      "Country-mean fill plus item-level missingness indicator; complete-case and MI reported alongside",
      "Weighted CRE-Mundlak estimation with country and country-year random intercepts"),
    n_after = c(sprintf("%s respondents", format(N_RESPONDENTS_FULL, big.mark=",")),
                sprintf("%d catalogue items", nrow(CAT)),
                sprintf("%d excluded as high-proximity", CAT[proximity=="high", .N]),
                "-", sprintf("%d items retained", length(INCLUDED)),
                sprintf("%s country-years", format(nrow(CY), big.mark=",")),
                sprintf("%d within + %d between terms", length(W_VARS), length(B_VARS)),
                "-", sprintf("%s respondents, %d countries",
                             format(nrow(ANA), big.mark=","), uniqueN(ANA$iso3))),
    threshold_applied = c("-","-","proximity == 'high'","codebook vmin/vmax + direction",
      sprintf("n_cyears >= %s; n_countries >= %s; within_sd >= %s",
              CFG$min_cyears_item, CFG$min_countries_item, CFG$min_within_sd),
      "-","-", sprintf("imputation = %s", CFG$imput_main),
      sprintf("FDR alpha = %s", CFG$fdr_alpha)),
    reported_in = c("T00","T00, T00b","Section 3.3","T06b","T02","T01","T03","T13, T14","T03, T08"))
  # >>> THESIS Table 2 ("Data Pipeline: Stages, Sample Sizes, and Decision Rules") -- HIGH confidence (name match) <<<
  fwrite(tab, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T23_data_pipeline.csv")); tab
}, error=function(e){ message("T23 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

T24 <- tryCatch({
  tab <- data.table(
    decision = c("Correlated random effects (Mundlak) rather than fixed effects",
      "Predictors at country-year, outcome at respondent level",
      "Country-mean imputation with missingness flag as main specification",
      "Items individually rather than as domain composites",
      "High-proximity items excluded before estimation",
      "Benjamini-Hochberg within declared families",
      "Oster bounds computed at both levels",
      "Four holdout designs rather than one",
      "Level-separated features in the flexible model",
      "Reference-group centring tested three ways",
      "Sign diagnostic at both levels",
      "Respondent level added only for household income"),
    justification = c(
      "Fixed effects would discard all between-country information, half the question in a comparative literature",
      "Predictors are conditions of national context; keeping the outcome individual preserves the structure the ICC shows is required",
      "An imputed cell takes its country mean, so its within deviation is exactly zero and cannot manufacture within-country association",
      "Reliability screening licensed aggregation for only some domains; composites elsewhere would impose structure the data do not support",
      "An item that restates the outcome inflates fit without identifying a condition of life",
      "Testing many candidates uniformly requires multiplicity control; declaring families in advance prevents post hoc family construction",
      "Applied within-only, a between-country association would read as unscreened rather than screened and passed",
      "A random split tests interpolation only; country, temporal and development holdouts test the generalisations that matter",
      "Without separating components, level-of-analysis conflation can be asserted but not demonstrated",
      "The attribution of a relative-position effect depends on how the reference group is defined",
      "Collinearity among structurally clustered national characteristics can reverse a between coefficient without reversing a within one",
      "Evaluative items share momentary state with the outcome within a single interview; country-year averaging washes this out but an individual comparison cannot"),
    consequence_if_ignored = c(
      "Between-country gradients would be unestimable",
      "Individual variance would be absorbed rather than quantified",
      "Systematic non-fielding would be concealed through sample restriction",
      "Composite scores would report reliability the items do not have",
      "The strongest predictor would be a paraphrase of the dependent variable",
      "A quarter of nominally significant associations would be reported as findings",
      "Between-country associations would read as more robust than within-country ones",
      "Out-of-sample performance would be overstated by interpolation",
      "Proposition 2 would be untestable",
      "A single arbitrary grouping would be presented as the relative-income effect",
      "Partialling artefacts would be interpreted as substantive reversals",
      "Same-method bias would be reported as a substantive individual-level association"),
    evidence = c("mundlak_test, T08","ICC, T21","T13, T14, T02","T06, T07, T08","Section 3.3",
                 "T03, Q4","T09","T16","T17, F06","T20, F12","T03b","T27, Section 3.9"))
  fwrite(tab, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T24_methodological_decisions.csv")); tab
}, error=function(e){ message("T24 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

T25 <- tryCatch({
  tab <- copy(CAT)[, .(code, label, domain, proximity, n_cat, vmin, vmax, direction)]
  tab[, tipo := fifelse(proximity=="structural","Objective (recorded fact)",
               fifelse(proximity=="perceptual","Subjective (evaluative judgment)",
                       "Excluded: too close to the outcome"))]

  tab[, reason_if_excluded := fifelse(entered_model, "",

# ============================================================================
# SECTION 16c: VARIANCE ACCOUNTING BY BLOCK  (what explains what)
# ============================================================================
# Replaces a residual ("about 60% is individual") with an explicit accounting:
# how much each block adds, and how much is left for factors the survey does
# not field. Checkpointed after every model so a failure mid-way still leaves
# the completed steps on disk.
VARACC <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("DT_IND"), "ln_income_h" %in% names(DT_IND), exists("CY"))
  d <- DT_IND[, .(iso3, year, wt, ln_income_h)]
  d[, grp_mean := weighted.mean(ln_income_h, wt, na.rm=TRUE), by=.(iso3, year)]
  ctrl_have <- intersect(CONTROLS, names(DT_IND))
  AKb <- DT_IND[, c("iso3","year","wt", OUTCOME, ctrl_have), with=FALSE]
  AKb[, ln_income_h_p := d$ln_income_h - d$grp_mean]
  setnames(AKb, OUTCOME, "cantril")
  AK <- merge(AKb, CY[, c("iso3","year", W_VARS, B_VARS, M_VARS), with=FALSE],
              by=c("iso3","year"))
  AK[, `:=`(iso3=factor(iso3), yearf=factor(year), cy=factor(paste(iso3, year, sep="_")))]
  AK <- AK[complete.cases(AK[, c("cantril","wt","ln_income_h_p", ctrl_have), with=FALSE])]
  stopifnot(nrow(AK) > 1000)

  BLOCKS <- list(sociodemographic=ctrl_have, relative_income="ln_income_h_p",
                 country_year=c(W_VARS, B_VARS))
  # r2_marginal() from the pipeline (Nakagawa & Schielzeth 2013): same definition
  # used by the rest of the tables, without adding dependencies.
  fit_r2 <- function(tv) {
    rhs <- if (length(tv)==0) "1" else paste(tv, collapse=" + ")
    f <- as.formula(paste("cantril ~", rhs, "+ (1|iso3) + (1|cy)"))
    m <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
           lmer(f, data=AK, weights=wt, REML=FALSE, control=CTRL_FAST))),
          error=function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(m)) return(list(r2m=NA_real_, r2c=NA_real_))
    list(r2m=tryCatch(as.numeric(r2_marginal(m)), error=function(e) NA_real_),
         r2c=tryCatch({
           vf <- var(as.vector(lme4::getME(m,"X") %*% lme4::fixef(m)))
           vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(m))
           as.numeric((vf + sum(vc$vcov[vc$grp!="Residual"])) / (vf + sum(vc$vcov)))
         }, error=function(e) NA_real_))
  }
  # Two entry orders: with correlated blocks (education with income) the
  # attributed contribution depends on order, so both are reported along with the range.
  ORDERS <- list(demog_first=c("sociodemographic","relative_income","country_year"),
                 income_first=c("relative_income","sociodemographic","country_year"))
  rows <- list(); i <- 0
  for (onm in names(ORDERS)) {
    acc <- character(0); prev <- fit_r2(character(0)); i <- i + 1
    rows[[i]] <- data.table(order=onm, step=0L, block="(null: country + country-year only)",
                            r2_marginal=prev$r2m, r2_conditional=prev$r2c, increment=NA_real_)
    for (k in seq_along(ORDERS[[onm]])) {
      bn <- ORDERS[[onm]][k]; acc <- c(acc, BLOCKS[[bn]]); cur <- fit_r2(acc); i <- i + 1
      rows[[i]] <- data.table(order=onm, step=k, block=bn, r2_marginal=cur$r2m,
                              r2_conditional=cur$r2c, increment=cur$r2m - prev$r2m)
      prev <- cur
      fwrite(rbindlist(rows), file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T21_variance_accounting.csv"))
      message(sprintf("    variance decomposition: %s step %d/%d (%s) saved", onm, k, length(ORDERS[[onm]]), bn))
    }
  }
  VA <- rbindlist(rows)
  RANGE <- VA[!is.na(increment), .(contrib_min=min(increment, na.rm=TRUE),
                                    contrib_max=max(increment, na.rm=TRUE)), by=block]
  fwrite(RANGE, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T21b_block_contribution_range.csv"))

  base_r2c <- VA[order=="demog_first" & step==0, r2_conditional]
  best <- VA[order=="demog_first" & !is.na(increment)]
  resid_val <- max(0, 1 - (base_r2c + sum(best$increment, na.rm=TRUE)))
  gr <- function(b){ r <- RANGE[block==b]
    if (!nrow(r)) "n/a" else sprintf("%.1f-%.1f%%", 100*r$contrib_min, 100*r$contrib_max) }
  VARACC_S <- sprintf(
    "Decomposing the variance in life evaluation by block clarifies what an account built from these data can reach. The country and country-year random structure accounts for %.1f%% of total variance; who the respondent is (age, sex, education, marital status, children) adds %s; their income position relative to same-year compatriots adds %s; and the full battery of %d national conditions adds %s. Because these blocks are correlated, each contribution is reported as a range across the two entry orders tested rather than as a single figure. The remaining %.1f%% is not explained by any measured variable: it is the share attributable to factors the survey does not field, personality dispositions, biography, life events and health among them. This is the structural ceiling of the design rather than a deficiency of the specification, and it reframes the modest R-squared values reported throughout as the honest limit of explaining evaluative well-being from conditions of life rather than from individual history.",
    100*base_r2c, gr("sociodemographic"), gr("relative_income"),
    length(INCLUDED), gr("country_year"), 100*resid_val)
  message(VARACC_S)

  ## ---- FIG 11: variance cascade ----
  nice <- c(sociodemographic="Who the respondent is\n(age, sex, education,\nmarital status, children)",
            relative_income ="Their income position\nrelative to same-year compatriots",
            country_year    =sprintf("National conditions\n(%d country-year predictors)", length(INCLUDED)))
  WF <- rbindlist(list(
    data.table(part="Where you live, and when\n(country + country-year)", value=base_r2c, kind="structure"),
    best[, .(part=nice[block], value=increment, kind="explained")],
    data.table(part="Unexplained\n(not fielded in the survey:\npersonality, biography,\nlife events, health)",
               value=resid_val, kind="residual")))
  WF[, part := factor(part, levels=rev(part))][, pct := 100*value]
  f11 <- ggplot(WF, aes(part, pct, fill=kind)) +
    geom_col(width=.66) +
    geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)), hjust=-.16, size=3.9,
              family="serif", fontface="bold", colour=PAL$ink) +
    coord_flip(clip="off") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,.2)), labels=function(x) paste0(x,"%")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=c(structure=PAL$between, explained=PAL$within,
                               residual=PAL$neutral), guide="none") +
    labs(title="Where the variance in life evaluation actually lives",
         subtitle="Share of total variance in the Cantril ladder accounted for by each block, entered in sequence.\nThe bottom bar is the ceiling of any account built from these data: it is what the survey does not measure,\nnot what fails to matter.",
         x=NULL, y="Share of total variance in life evaluation",
         caption=sprintf("Nested mixed models, N = %s respondents. Marginal R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth 2013) for fixed-effect blocks;\nconditional R-squared for the country and country-year random structure. Blocks are correlated, so any single\nattribution depends on entry order: T21b reports the range across both orders tested.",
                         format(nrow(AK), big.mark=","))) +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=9.2, lineheight=.95), panel.grid.major.y=element_blank())
  # >>> THESIS Figure 3 ("Variance in Life Evaluation by Level of Analysis") -- HIGH confidence <<<
sv(f11, "F11_variance_accounting.png", 9.8, 6.4)
  list(table=VA, range=RANGE, sentence=VARACC_S, n=nrow(AK))
}, error=function(e){ message("VARACC skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })


## ---- FIG 12: reference-group sensitivity ----
F12 <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(!is.null(REFSENS))
  S20 <- copy(REFSENS$table)
  S20[, ref_nice := fifelse(reference_group=="country_year","vs. all compatriots",
               fifelse(reference_group=="age_country_year","vs. same-age peers",
                       "vs. same-age, same-education peers"))]
  S20[, spec_nice := fifelse(grepl("^full", spec),"Net of all national conditions",
                                                  "Net of sociodemographics only")]
  S20[, ref_nice := factor(ref_nice, levels=rev(c("vs. all compatriots","vs. same-age peers",
                                                   "vs. same-age, same-education peers")))]
  f12 <- ggplot(S20, aes(estimate, ref_nice, colour=spec_nice)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept=0, colour=PAL$rule, linewidth=.6) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin=conf.low, xmax=conf.high), height=.14, linewidth=1,
                   position=position_dodge(width=.5)) +
    geom_point(size=3.4, position=position_dodge(width=.5)) +
    geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.3f", estimate)), position=position_dodge(width=.5),
              vjust=-1.25, size=3.1, family="serif", show.legend=FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=c(`Net of all national conditions`=PAL$between,
                                  `Net of sociodemographics only`=PAL$within)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,.12))) +
    labs(title="Relative income: the same answer, whoever you compare people to",
         subtitle="Coefficient on a respondent's income position relative to their reference group, estimated three ways and\nunder two control sets. The estimate barely moves, so the association is not an artefact of either choice.",
         x="Coefficient on relative income position (Cantril points)", y=NULL, colour=NULL,
         caption="Repeated cross-section, not a panel: this compares different people surveyed at the same time, never the same\nperson over time, and supports no claim about within-person change. Bars are 95% confidence intervals, narrow\ngiven the sample size. Reference-group centring follows Enders & Tofighi (2007).") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=9.5), panel.grid.major.y=element_blank(),
          legend.position="top")
  # >>> THESIS Figure 11 ("Relative Income Under Three Definitions of the Reference Group") -- HIGH confidence <<<
sv(f12, "F12_relative_income_sensitivity.png", 9.8, 5.6); TRUE
}, error=function(e){ message("F12 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })


## ---- FIG 13: the three-level architecture ----
F13 <- tryCatch({
  icc_c  <- ICC$country; icc_cy <- ICC$country_year
  stopifnot(is.finite(icc_c), is.finite(icc_cy))
  ARCH <- data.table(
    level = factor(c("Country","Country-year","Respondent"),
                   levels=c("Respondent","Country-year","Country")),
    share = c(icc_c, max(0, icc_cy - icc_c), max(0, 1 - icc_cy)),
    answers = c("Which conditions distinguish\ncountries from each other",
                "Whether life evaluation moves\nas a country changes",
                "Differences between people\nsurveyed at the same time"))
  ARCH[, pct := 100*share]
  f13 <- ggplot(ARCH, aes(level, pct, fill=level)) +
    geom_col(width=.58) +
    geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)), hjust=-.14, size=4.1,
              family="serif", fontface="bold", colour=PAL$ink) +
    geom_text(aes(y=0, label=answers), hjust=0, vjust=2.9, size=3.0,
              family="serif", colour=PAL$neutral, lineheight=.95) +
    coord_flip(clip="off") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,.34)), labels=function(x) paste0(x,"%")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=c(Respondent=PAL$neutral, `Country-year`=PAL$within,
                               Country=PAL$between), guide="none") +
    labs(title="Three levels, three different questions",
         subtitle="Variance in life evaluation partitioned by the unconditional model. Each level enters the specification through\nits own terms and answers a question the other two cannot. Conflating them is the error the design prevents.",
         x=NULL, y="Share of variance in life evaluation",
         caption=sprintf("Intraclass correlations from the unconditional model: %.3f at country level, %.3f cumulative at country-year level.\nSee T22 for what each level can and cannot support, and F11 for how much of the respondent-level share is measured.",
                         icc_c, icc_cy)) +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text.y=element_text(size=10.5, face="bold"),
          panel.grid.major.y=element_blank(), plot.margin=margin(14,20,12,14))
  sv(f13, "F13_level_architecture.png", 10.5, 6.4); TRUE
}, error=function(e){ message("F13 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })


# ============================================================================
# SECTION 16d: LEVEL-OF-ANALYSIS FIGURES, INCLUDING THE RESPONDENT LAYER
# ============================================================================
# Figures F01-F13 operate at the country or country-year level. This block adds
# the individual layer to the visual argument and turns into images the
# contrasts that until now existed only in tables (T27, T16, T17, T18). Each
# figure runs in its own tryCatch: a failure in one does not take down the rest.

# LEVEL palette, consistent across the block. The individual layer gets its own
# colour so it is distinguishable from the two the rest of the report already uses.
LVL_COL <- c(respondent = "#B25A3A", within = PAL$within,
             between = PAL$between, `missing flag` = "grey70")
LVL_LAB <- c(respondent = "Respondent (individual)",
             within  = "Within-country (change over time)",
             between = "Between-country (national gradient)",
             `missing flag` = "Missingness flag")

lbl_of <- function(dt) {
  d <- copy(dt)
  d[, code := gsub("_(w|b|p|miss)$", "", feature)]
  d <- merge(d, unique(CAT[, .(code, label)]), by = "code", all.x = TRUE)
  d[code == "ln_gdp",      label := "GDP per capita (log)"]
  d[code == "ln_income_h", label := "Household income (log)"]
  d[is.na(label), label := code]
  d[]
}

## ---- F14: permutation importance, the THREE layers competing ----
tryCatch({
  stopifnot(!is.null(ML3), nrow(ML3$pi) > 0)
  P <- lbl_of(ML3$pi)[level != "missing flag"]
  TOP <- head(P[order(-importance)], 18)
  TOP[, disp := paste0(label, "  (", fifelse(level=="respondent","individual",
                       fifelse(level=="within","within","between")), ")")]
  TOP[, disp := factor(disp, levels = rev(disp))]
  f14 <- ggplot(TOP, aes(disp, importance, fill = level)) +
    geom_col(width = .72) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(0, importance - sd), ymax = importance + sd),
                  width = .22, linewidth = .35, colour = PAL$ink, alpha = .55) +
    coord_flip(clip = "off") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = LVL_COL, labels = LVL_LAB, name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .08))) +
    labs(title = "One model, three levels of variation, three different answers",
         subtitle = "Permutation importance on the country holdout, with each predictor's between-country, within-country and\nindividual components entered as separate features. National income dominates between countries; a respondent's\nincome position relative to their own compatriots ranks second overall, far above income change within countries.",
         x = NULL, y = "Permutation importance (increase in out-of-sample error when shuffled)",
         caption = "Error bars are one standard deviation across permutation repetitions. Only the eighteen most important features are shown.\nBecause the components enter as distinct features, the contrast is demonstrated by the model rather than asserted.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.6),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
  sv(f14, "F14_importance_three_levels.png", 11, 8)
}, error=function(e){ message("F14 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)) })

## ---- F15: rank slopegraph across levels ----
# The crossing lines ARE the conflation error, drawn out.
tryCatch({
  S <- PI[level %chin% c("within","between")]
  stopifnot(nrow(S) > 0)
  S <- copy(S)
  S[, rank_in_level := frank(-importance, ties.method="first"), by = level]
  keep <- S[, .(best = min(rank_in_level)), by = code][order(best)][1:14, code]
  S <- S[code %chin% keep]
  S[code == "ln_gdp", label := "GDP per capita (log)"]
  S[is.na(label), label := code]
  S[, level := factor(level, levels = c("between","within"))]
  S[, is_gdp := code == "ln_gdp"]
  f15 <- ggplot(S, aes(level, rank_in_level, group = code)) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = is_gdp, linewidth = is_gdp), alpha = .78) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = is_gdp), size = 2.3) +
    geom_text(data = S[level=="between"], aes(label = label), hjust = 1.08,
              size = 2.85, family = "serif", colour = PAL$ink) +
    geom_text(data = S[level=="within"], aes(label = paste0("#", rank_in_level)),
              hjust = -.6, size = 2.85, family = "serif", colour = PAL$neutral) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = c(1,5,10,15,20,25,30)) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(mult = c(.42,.18)),
                     labels = c(between="Read between countries", within="Read within countries")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE`=PAL$between, `FALSE`="grey62"), guide="none") +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`TRUE`=1.5, `FALSE`=.6), guide="none") +
    labs(title = "The ranking a predictor gets depends on the level it is read at",
         subtitle = "Each line is one condition of life, connecting its rank by permutation importance across countries (left) with its rank\nwithin countries over time (right). Crossing lines are the level-of-analysis error made visible: an analyst who does not\nseparate the components reads a single ranking that belongs to neither. GDP per capita is highlighted.",
         x = NULL, y = "Rank by permutation importance (1 = most important)",
         caption = "Only the fourteen predictors reaching the highest rank at either level are shown, for legibility.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10))
  sv(f15, "F15_rank_slopegraph.png", 9.5, 8)
}, error=function(e){ message("F15 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)) })

tryCatch({

               hi = r$conf.high[1], level = lv) }
  D <- rbindlist(Filter(Negate(is.null), list(
    pick("ln_gdp_b","National income, across countries\n(GDP per capita, between)","between"),
    pick("ln_gdp_w","National income, over time\n(GDP per capita, within)","within"),
    pick("ln_income_h_b","Household income, across countries\n(between)","between"),
    pick("ln_income_h_w","Household income, over time\n(within)","within"))))
  if (!is.null(REFSENS)) {
    r <- REFSENS$table[reference_group=="country_year"][1]
    if (nrow(r) && !is.na(r$estimate))
      D <- rbind(D, data.table(what="Household income RELATIVE to\nsame-country-year peers (individual)",
                               est=r$estimate, lo=r$conf.low, hi=r$conf.high,

  }
  stopifnot(nrow(D) > 0)
  D[, what := factor(what, levels = rev(what))]
  f17 <- ggplot(D, aes(est, what, colour = level)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$rule, linewidth = .6) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = .16, linewidth = .95, na.rm=TRUE) +
    geom_point(size = 3.4) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", est)), vjust = -1.15, size = 3.05,
              family = "serif", show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = LVL_COL, labels = LVL_LAB, name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "Income is associated with life evaluation in different ways at each level",
         subtitle = "Adjusted associations in Cantril points for national income between countries, national change within countries,\nhousehold income, and a respondent's position relative to same-year compatriots. The figure separates these estimands\nrather than treating them as a single income effect.",
         x = "Coefficient (Cantril ladder points)", y = NULL,
         caption = "Bars are 95% confidence intervals. The relative-position estimate compares different people surveyed at the same time,\nnot the same person over time: the survey is a repeated cross-section, so no within-person claim is supported.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position="top", axis.text.y = element_text(size=8.8, lineheight=.95),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

## ---- F22: precision of the nulls (absence of evidence != evidence of absence) ----
tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("SESOI"), is.finite(SESOI))
  NL <- COEF[level=="within" & sig_fdr==FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(NL) > 0)
  NL <- merge(NL, unique(CAT[, .(code, label)]), by="code", all.x=TRUE)
  NL[code=="ln_gdp", label := "GDP per capita (log)"]
  NL[is.na(label), label := code]
  NL[, precise := conf.low > -SESOI & conf.high < SESOI]
  NL[, label := factor(label, levels = NL[order(estimate), label])]
  f22 <- ggplot(NL, aes(estimate, label, colour = precise)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -SESOI, xmax = SESOI, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = PAL$rule, alpha = .22) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = .0, linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL$within, `FALSE` = PAL$neutral),
                        labels = c(`TRUE` = "Precise null: rules out effects of interest",
                                   `FALSE` = "Inconclusive: still compatible with them"), name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "Not established is not the same as does not matter",
         subtitle = sprintf("Within-country predictors that do not survive multiplicity correction, with 95%% confidence intervals. The shaded band\nis the smallest effect confirmed anywhere in the catalogue (|%.3f| Cantril points). An interval falling entirely inside it\nwould rule out an effect of comparable size; an interval crossing it cannot.", SESOI),
         x = "Within-country coefficient (Cantril points)", y = NULL,
         caption = "This is an equivalence-style reading of null results: the question is not whether an estimate reached significance, but\nwhether the data were precise enough to exclude an effect worth caring about.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.8),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
  # >>> THESIS Figure 5 ("Precision of the Non-Established Within-Country Results") -- HIGH confidence <<<
sv(f22, "F22_informative_nulls.png", 10, 8)
}, error=function(e){ message("F22 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)) })

    OW <- rbind(OW, O[!is.na(beta_controlled_b),
                      .(code, b = beta_controlled_b, bs = beta_star_b,

  OW <- merge(OW, unique(CAT[, .(code, label)]), by="code", all.x=TRUE)
  OW[code=="ln_gdp", label := "GDP per capita (log)"]
  OW[is.na(label), label := code]
  OW <- OW[!is.na(bs)]
  stopifnot(nrow(OW) > 0)
  ordv <- OW[level=="within"][order(abs(b)), label]
  OW[, label := factor(label, levels = unique(c(ordv, setdiff(OW$label, ordv))))]
  f23 <- ggplot(OW, aes(y = label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = b, xend = bs, yend = label, colour = robust), linewidth = .8, alpha = .85) +
    geom_point(aes(x = b, colour = robust), size = 2.1) +
    geom_point(aes(x = bs, colour = robust), size = 1.5, shape = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ level, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL$within, `FALSE` = PAL$between),
                        labels = c(`TRUE` = "Bounded away from zero",
                                   `FALSE` = "Bounding set includes zero"), name = NULL, na.value = "grey70") +
    labs(title = "How much unobserved confounding would it take to explain the estimate away?",
         subtitle = "Filled points are the adjusted coefficient; hollow points the Oster bound implied by equal selection on unobservables.\nThe segment between them is the bounding set. Where that set does not cross zero, the association survives the\namount of omitted-variable bias the observed controls would imply.",
         x = "Coefficient (Cantril points)", y = NULL,
         caption = "Oster (2019) bounds quantify exposure to time-varying confounding rather than removing it. Bounds are computed at\nboth levels from the same uncontrolled fit, so a between-country association is screened rather than merely unscreened.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.2),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

         x = NULL, y = "Number of predictors",
         caption = "Predictors dropped at the screening stage are not judged unimportant: they are conditions the data cannot speak to,\neither because they were not fielded widely enough or because they do not move within countries over time.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8.4, lineheight = .95),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
  # >>> THESIS Figure 4 ("From a Theoretical Catalogue to an Evidence Map") -- HIGH confidence (title is near-verbatim) <<<
sv(f24, "F24_catalogue_funnel.png", 10, 6)
}, error=function(e){ message("F24 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)) })

## ---- F25: the three models, the four designs ----
tryCatch({
  # >>> FIX (reproducibility audit): VALID is built from RES (see line ~2319),
  # the same object that empties out under QUICK = TRUE when every design in
  # run_split() fails its minimum-row guard (see F26's stopifnot below, which
  # is what originally surfaced this). Without this check, F25 previously had
  # no defence against that case: melt()/ggplot() on a 0-row VALID does not
  # throw, so the figure would render blank or malformed with no warning at
  # all -- a silent failure, worse than F26's loud one. <<<
  stopifnot(nrow(VALID) > 0)
  V <- melt(VALID[, .(design, r2_linear, r2_enet, r2_xgb)], id.vars = "design",
            variable.name = "model", value.name = "r2")
  V[, model := factor(model, levels = c("r2_linear","r2_enet","r2_xgb"),
                      labels = c("Linear (the specification)","Elastic net (shrinkage)","Gradient boosting (flexible)"))]
  V[, design := factor(design, levels = c("random","country","temporal","development"),
                       labels = c("Random split","Unseen countries","Future waves","Unseen development stratum"))]
  f25 <- ggplot(V, aes(design, r2, fill = model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .72), width = .62) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", r2)), position = position_dodge(width = .72),
              vjust = fifelse(V$r2 >= 0, -.5, 1.4), size = 2.7, family = "serif") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(PAL$ink, PAL$neutral, PAL$within), name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "Three model families, four ways of holding data out",
         subtitle = "Out-of-sample R-squared on identical held-out rows. The three families track each other closely everywhere except\nthe development holdout, where the flexible model fits structure that does not transport. Regularisation adds\nalmost nothing, indicating the linear specification is not over-parameterised for this predictor set.",
         x = NULL, y = "Out-of-sample R-squared",
         caption = "A negative value means the model predicts the held-out group worse than that group's own mean would.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9))
  # >>> THESIS Figure 13 ("Out-of-Sample Prediction Under Increasingly Demanding Transport Tests") -- HIGH confidence <<<
sv(f25, "F25_three_models_four_designs.png", 10.5, 6)
}, error=function(e){ message("F25 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)) })

## ---- F26: the boosting learning curve ----
tryCatch({
  logs <- rbindlist(lapply(names(RES), function(nm) {
    el <- RES[[nm]]$eval_log
    if (is.null(el) || !nrow(el)) return(NULL)
    vc <- setdiff(names(el), "iter")[1]
    data.table(design = nm, iter = el$iter, rmse = el[[vc]],
               best = RES[[nm]]$row$best_iter)
  }))
  stopifnot(nrow(logs) > 0)
  logs[, design := factor(design, levels = c("random","country","temporal","development"))]
  f26 <- ggplot(logs, aes(iter, rmse, colour = design)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_vline(data = unique(logs[, .(design, best)]), aes(xintercept = best, colour = design),
               linetype = "22", linewidth = .5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "D", end = .85, name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "The flexible model stops where the held-out data tell it to",
         subtitle = "Validation error by boosting round, with the early-stopping point marked for each design. The number of trees is\nchosen by held-out performance rather than fixed in advance, so the comparison against the linear specification\nis not a matter of how hard each model was tuned.",
         x = "Boosting round", y = "Validation RMSE",
         caption = "Early stopping halts training once held-out error stops improving for a fixed number of rounds. Curves that flatten\nearly indicate little additional structure for the flexible model to recover.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  sv(f26, "F26_boosting_learning_curves.png", 10, 6)
}, error=function(e){ message("F26 skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)) })

## ---- F27: importance aggregated by thematic domain and level ----
tryCatch({

         x = NULL, y = "Summed permutation importance",

## ---- F31: sensitivity to the imputation strategy ----
tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("IMP_TAB"), nrow(IMP_TAB) > 0)

            variable.name = "strategy", value.name = "est")
  M <- M[!is.na(est)]
  M[, strategy := factor(strategy, levels = mcols,
      labels = c(country_mean = "Country-mean fill + flag (main)",

  ordl <- M[strategy == levels(M$strategy)[1]][order(est), label]
  M[, label := factor(label, levels = ordl)]
  f31 <- ggplot(M, aes(est, label, colour = strategy, shape = strategy)) +

    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15), name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "The within-country estimates do not depend on how missing data are handled",
         subtitle = "Within-country coefficients under three missing-data strategies. Country-mean filling with a missingness flag is the\nmain specification; complete-case analysis makes no assumption about missing values; multiple imputation uses the\ncovariance among predictors. Where the three agree, the estimate is not an artefact of the imputation choice.",
         x = "Within-country coefficient (Cantril points)", y = NULL,
         caption = "An imputed cell takes its country mean, so its within-country deviation is exactly zero and it cannot manufacture a\nwithin-country association. Divergence across strategies would indicate sensitivity to non-random fielding.") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.6),

#| cache: false
# ============================================================================

# Thesis 4.11: "all narrative statements referencing numerical results are

SENTENCES <- list(
