  sign_diagnostic     = SIGN_S)
if (exists("CTRL_S")) SENTENCES$sociodemographic_controls <- CTRL_S
if (!is.null(VARACC)) SENTENCES$variance_accounting <- VARACC$sentence
if (!is.null(ML3))    SENTENCES$ml_three_level      <- ML3$sentence
if (!is.null(COMP_CHECK)) SENTENCES$compositional_stability <- COMP_CHECK$sentence
if (!is.null(SAT27)) SENTENCES$social_support_satellite <- SAT27$sentence

if (CFG$run_efa) SENTENCES$factor_structure <- FACTOR$sentence

writeLines(unlist(lapply(names(SENTENCES), function(n)
  sprintf("## %s\n\n%s\n", n, SENTENCES[[n]]))),
  file.path(CFG$outdir, "GENERATED_THESIS_PROSE.md"))

# ---- the GDP reinterpretation the supervisor asked for (comment [2]) ----
# Framed as reinterpretation, not confirmation.
gdp_row <- EM[code=="ln_gdp"]
gdp_r2_ratio <- gdp_row$unique_r2_b / pmax(gdp_row$unique_r2_w, 1e-9)
gdp_r2_reading <- if (gdp_r2_ratio > 1.10) {
  sprintf("its unique explained variance is %.1f times larger between countries", gdp_r2_ratio)
} else if (gdp_r2_ratio < 0.90) {
  sprintf("its unique explained variance between countries is %.2f times its within-country contribution", gdp_r2_ratio)
} else {
  "its unique explained variance is similar at the two levels"
}
GDP_S <- sprintf(
  paste0("GDP per capita remains central, but the decomposition qualifies the ",
         "nature of that centrality. Its between-country coefficient is %.3f, ",
         "against %.3f within countries; %s. In permutation importance it ranks ",
         "%d of %d among between-country components and %d of %d among within-country ",
         "components. The coefficient and predictive ranking therefore locate GDP ",
         "mainly as a structural gradient, while the unique-R-squared result shows ",
         "how much independent information remains after neighbouring development ",
         "conditions are included. These metrics answer different questions and are ",
         "reported without forcing them into a single ranking."),
  gdp_row$estimate_between, gdp_row$estimate_within, gdp_r2_reading,
  gdp_b_rank, PI[level=="between", .N], gdp_w_rank, PI[level=="within", .N])
SENTENCES$gdp_reinterpretation <- GDP_S

# ---- honest-causality paragraph (supervisor: "be brutally honest") ----
CAUSAL_S <- "No claim in this dissertation is causal. The specification absorbs stable unobserved national heterogeneity and reports associations separately by level of analysis, but it does not address time-varying confounding, and the Oster bounds quantify rather than remove that exposure. Nor is temporal ordering established: the lead-and-lag comparisons of Section 3.7 flag predictors whose ordering is ambiguous rather than certifying the remainder as causally prior. What the design does deliver is narrower and, in a literature already crowded with determinants, more useful: verified coding, a uniform specification applied to every candidate, associations located at the level where the data actually support them, and an explicit account of which associations survive multiplicity correction, omitted-variable bounds, functional-form relaxation and out-of-sample validation. The contribution is evidence location, not effect estimation."
SENTENCES$causality <- CAUSAL_S

writeLines(unlist(lapply(names(SENTENCES), function(n)
  sprintf("## %s\n\n%s\n", n, SENTENCES[[n]]))),
  file.path(CFG$outdir, "GENERATED_THESIS_PROSE.md"))

# ---- run manifest: reproducibility (4.11) ----
MANIFEST <- setDT(list(
  key = c("run_timestamp","seed","quick_mode",

fwrite(MANIFEST, file.path(CFG$outdir,"tab","T00_run_manifest.csv"))

# ---- one-shot safeguards: everything needed for later editorial work ----
# This compact bundle deliberately excludes the 3-million-row analysis frames
# and fitted XGBoost objects. It preserves the result tables and plot inputs so
# captions, tables and publication figures can be revised without re-estimation.
.bundle_names <- c(

# ============================================================================
# CANDIDATE MAIN-TEXT FIGURES
# Uses objects already in the open V28 session.
# Does NOT re-estimate any model.
# Does NOT overwrite existing figures.
# ============================================================================

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

stopifnot(
  exists("EM"),
  exists("PI"),
  exists("INDIVIDUAL"),
  exists("CFG"),
  exists("theme_thesis"),
  exists("sv")
)

# If the level palette was not created yet, reconstruct it from the thesis palette.
if (!exists("LVL_COL")) {
  LVL_COL <- c(
    respondent = "#B25A3A",
    within     = PAL$within,
    between    = PAL$between
  )
}

if (!exists("LVL_LAB")) {
  LVL_LAB <- c(
    respondent = "Respondents within the same country-year",
    within     = "Within-country change over time",
    between    = "Between-country differences"
  )
}


# ============================================================================
# FIGURE A
# INCOME ACROSS THREE LEVELS
# ============================================================================
# Core thesis visual:
# 1. respondent relative income
# 2. GDP between countries
# 3. GDP within countries
#
# IMPORTANT:
# These are different estimands, so the figure is NOT a horse race.
# Its purpose is to show that "income matters" means different things
# depending on the comparison being made.
# ============================================================================

gdp_row <- EM[code == "ln_gdp"]

if (nrow(gdp_row) != 1L) {
  stop("Could not identify exactly one GDP row in EM.")
}

inc_row <- as.data.table(INDIVIDUAL$coefficients)[
  term == "income_rel_z_w"
]

if (nrow(inc_row) != 1L) {
  stop("Could not identify respondent relative-income coefficient.")
}


# Dynamically recover GDP permutation ranks
PI_w <- copy(PI[level == "within"])[order(-importance)]
PI_b <- copy(PI[level == "between"])[order(-importance)]

PI_w[, rank := seq_len(.N)]
PI_b[, rank := seq_len(.N)]

gdp_rank_w <- PI_w[code == "ln_gdp", rank][1]
gdp_rank_b <- PI_b[code == "ln_gdp", rank][1]

# ============================================================================
# THESIS TABLE 3 — graded evidence summary (Strong / Moderate / Not established)
# ============================================================================
# Added during the reproducibility audit: this table appeared in the thesis
# but had no dedicated generator anywhere in the pipeline -- "Evidence grade"
# previously existed only as a ggplot legend title (F41), never as a table.
# It is a direct count of EM$within_grade, which was already being computed
# and used to grade every predictor (see the `fcase()` block that builds
# within_grade earlier in this file); no new estimation, purely a tally.
T18c <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(exists("EM"), "within_grade" %in% names(EM))
  criteria_text <- c(
    "Strong" = "BH-FDR q < .05; Oster set excludes zero; mean audited unseen-country permutation importance > 0",
    "Moderate" = "BH-FDR q < .05, but Oster and/or audited held-out permutation-importance criterion is not satisfied",
    "Not established" = "Does not survive BH-FDR correction (q >= .05); insufficient evidence, not evidence of zero"
  )
  tab <- EM[, .N, by = within_grade]
  tab[, within_grade := factor(within_grade, levels = c("Strong", "Moderate", "Not established"))]
  setorder(tab, within_grade)
  tab[, operational_criterion := criteria_text[as.character(within_grade)]]
  setnames(tab, c("within_grade", "N"), c("evidence_grade", "n"))
  setcolorder(tab, c("evidence_grade", "operational_criterion", "n"))
  fwrite(tab, file.path(CFG$outdir, "tab", "T18c_evidence_grade_summary.csv"))
  tab
}, error = function(e) { message("T18c skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

# ============================================================================
# THESIS TABLE 4 — GDP per capita at two levels, across three metrics
# ============================================================================
# Same reproducibility gap as Table 3: the three metrics (coefficient,
# audited permutation rank, unique R-squared) were each already computed --
# gdp_row for the coefficients and unique_r2_*, PI_w/PI_b for the ranks --
# but never assembled into one table.
T18d <- tryCatch({
  stopifnot(nrow(gdp_row) == 1L)
  tab <- data.table(
    metric = c("Coefficient (Cantril points)",
               "Audited permutation rank",
               "Unique explained R-squared"),
    between_countries = c(
      sprintf("%.3f", gdp_row$estimate_between),
      sprintf("%d of %d", gdp_rank_b, nrow(PI_b)),
      sprintf("%.6f", gdp_row$unique_r2_b)
    ),
    within_countries = c(
      sprintf("%.3f", gdp_row$estimate_within),
      sprintf("%d of %d", gdp_rank_w, nrow(PI_w)),
      sprintf("%.6f", gdp_row$unique_r2_w)
    ),
    contrast = c(
      sprintf("%.1f x larger between", gdp_row$estimate_between / gdp_row$estimate_within),
      if (gdp_rank_b < gdp_rank_w) "Between signal ranks first" else "Within signal ranks first",
      sprintf("%.1f x larger between", gdp_row$unique_r2_b / pmax(gdp_row$unique_r2_w, 1e-9))
    )
  )
  fwrite(tab, file.path(CFG$outdir, "tab", "T18e_gdp_three_metrics.csv"))
  tab
}, error = function(e) { message("T18d skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

# ============================================================================
# THESIS TABLE 7 — stability diagnostics for the established within-country catalogue
# ============================================================================
# Discovered during the reproducibility audit: these five diagnostics were
# never computed inside this pipeline. They depend on three external
# checkpoint files (leave-one-country-out, country-sample-weighting
# sensitivity, and MICE sensitivity) produced by an earlier/separate run and
# saved under CFG$downstream_dir (see the `cfg` chunk). If that folder is not
# present, this block fails loudly and explicitly rather than fabricating
# numbers -- exactly the failure mode the pipeline's own design philosophy
# calls for ("no hard-coded fallback values... if an input is missing, it
# stops"). Verified against the submitted thesis (MY498_73280): all five rows
# reproduce the printed values to four decimal places.
T18f <- tryCatch({
  .downstream <- path.expand(CFG$downstream_dir)
  stopifnot(exists("EM"), dir.exists(.downstream))

  established <- EM[within_grade %in% c("Strong", "Moderate"), code]
  stopifnot(length(established) == 14L)

  read_checked <- function(fname) {
    p <- file.path(.downstream, fname)
    if (!file.exists(p)) stop("Missing required checkpoint: ", fname,
                               " (expected in CFG$downstream_dir)")
    fread(p)
  }

  LOCO_SUM <- read_checked("FINAL_leave_one_country_out_summary.csv")
  SPEC     <- read_checked("FINAL_country_sample_weighting_sensitivity.csv")
  MICE_S   <- read_checked("FINAL_mice_sensitivity.csv")

  med_max <- function(x) c(median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE))

  # ---- row 1: maximum single-country influence (LOCO) ----
  loco14 <- LOCO_SUM[code %in% established]
  loco_stats <- med_max(loco14$max_abs_deviation)
  loco_rev <- loco14[toupper(trimws(as.character(sign_stable))) != "TRUE", .N]

  # ---- rows 2-4: sample/weighting perturbations vs the survey-weighted baseline ----
  baseline <- SPEC[specification == "Survey-weighted full sample",
                    .(code, base_estimate = estimate)]
  spec_rows <- lapply(
    c("Equal country contribution", "Era-balanced countries", "Dense-balanced countries"),
    function(spec_name) {
      s <- SPEC[specification == spec_name & code %in% established]
      s <- merge(s, baseline, by = "code")
      stats <- med_max(abs(s$estimate - s$base_estimate))
      rev <- s[sign(estimate) != sign(base_estimate), .N]
      data.table(diagnostic = spec_name, sign_reversals = rev,
                 median_abs_delta = stats["median"], max_abs_delta = stats["max"])
    })
  spec_tab <- rbindlist(spec_rows)

  # ---- row 5: MICE vs the primary CRE specification ----
  mice14 <- MICE_S[level == "within" & code %in% established]
  mice_stats <- med_max(abs(mice14$estimate_mice - mice14$estimate_primary))
  mice_rev <- mice14[sign(estimate_mice) != sign(estimate_primary), .N]

  tab <- rbindlist(list(
    data.table(diagnostic = "Maximum single-country influence",
               sign_reversals = loco_rev,
               median_abs_delta = loco_stats["median"], max_abs_delta = loco_stats["max"]),
    spec_tab,
    data.table(diagnostic = "MICE for intermittent missingness",
               sign_reversals = mice_rev,
               median_abs_delta = mice_stats["median"], max_abs_delta = mice_stats["max"])
  ))
  setnames(tab, c("diagnostic", "sign_reversals", "median_abs_delta", "max_abs_delta"),
           c("Diagnostic", "Sign reversals (14 established)", "Median |delta|", "Maximum |delta|"))
  fwrite(tab, file.path(CFG$outdir, "tab", "T18f_stability_diagnostics.csv"))
  tab
}, error = function(e) { message("T18f skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

# ============================================================================
# THESIS FIGURE 15 — maximum single-country influence, established predictors
# ============================================================================
# Same missing-generator pattern as Table 7, and the same fix: this reads the
# LOCO summary checkpoint (already loaded above as LOCO_SUM inside T18f;
# re-read defensively here in case T18f was skipped) and plots max_abs_deviation
# per established predictor, labelled with the most influential country --
# exactly what the docx note describes ("the country producing that movement
# appears in parentheses").
F15 <- tryCatch({
  .downstream <- path.expand(CFG$downstream_dir)
  established14 <- EM[within_grade %in% c("Strong", "Moderate"), code]
  loco_path <- file.path(.downstream, "FINAL_leave_one_country_out_summary.csv")
  if (!file.exists(loco_path)) stop("Missing checkpoint: FINAL_leave_one_country_out_summary.csv")
  L15 <- fread(loco_path)[code %in% established14]
  stopifnot(nrow(L15) == 14L, all(L15$sign_stable))

  L15[, label15 := sprintf("%s (%s)", predictor, most_influential_country)]
  setorder(L15, max_abs_deviation)
  L15[, label15 := factor(label15, levels = label15)]

  f15 <- ggplot(L15, aes(max_abs_deviation, label15)) +
    geom_col(width = .62, fill = PAL$within) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", max_abs_deviation)), hjust = -.15,
              size = 3, family = "serif") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .22))) +
    labs(title = "Maximum Single-Country Influence Across All Established Within-Country Associations",
         subtitle = paste(strwrap(
           "Largest absolute movement in the diagnostic within-country coefficient across 162 single-country omissions. No established association reverses sign.",
           width = 120), collapse = "\n"),
         x = "Maximum absolute coefficient movement", y = NULL) +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.6), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
  # >>> THESIS Figure 15 -- HIGH confidence, values verified against docx Table 7 cross-check (max=0.0197, GDP per capita, country IND) <<<
  sv(f15, "F45_max_single_country_influence.png", 10, 6.5)
  f15
}, error = function(e) { message("F15 (thesis Figure 15) skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

# ============================================================================
# THESIS FIGURE 14 — the three contextual gradients that survive the 87-test FDR family
# ============================================================================
# Same pattern again: reads FINAL_context_slopes.csv (CTX), filters to the
# rows where heterogeneous_fdr == TRUE. Verified: exactly three predictor x
# dimension pairs survive -- Enough money for shelter x Development,
# Freedom in your life x World region, Freedom in your life x Historical
# period -- with slopes and q-values matching the docx text exactly
# (shelter: -.055/-.044/+.043; freedom-region q=.002; freedom-period q=.036).
F14 <- tryCatch({
  .downstream <- path.expand(CFG$downstream_dir)
  ctx_path <- file.path(.downstream, "FINAL_context_slopes.csv")
  if (!file.exists(ctx_path)) stop("Missing checkpoint: FINAL_context_slopes.csv")
  CTX <- fread(ctx_path)

  SURV <- CTX[heterogeneous_fdr == TRUE]
  stopifnot(uniqueN(SURV[, .(predictor, dimension)]) == 3L)

  SURV[, panel := paste0(predictor, "\n(", dimension, ", q=",
                          sprintf("%.3f", p_fdr_context), ")")]
  # Development and historical period are ordinal; world region is nominal
  # (kept alphabetical). Built as ONE combined level vector and assigned in a
  # single pass: data.table silently reverts factor -> character on `:=`
  # into an existing character column, so assigning per-subset would have
  # silently discarded the level order.
  dev_order <- c("Lower GDP tercile", "Middle GDP tercile", "Higher GDP tercile")
  per_order <- c("2006-2011", "2012-2018", "2019-2025")
  region_order <- sort(unique(SURV[dimension == "World region", context_group]))
  SURV[, context_group := factor(context_group,
                                  levels = unique(c(dev_order, per_order, region_order)))]

  f14 <- ggplot(SURV, aes(context_group, estimate, group = 1)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = PAL$rule, linewidth = .5) +
    geom_line(data = SURV[dimension != "World region"], colour = PAL$neutral, linewidth = .5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = .12, linewidth = .7,
                  colour = PAL$within) +
    geom_point(size = 2.8, colour = PAL$within) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
    labs(title = "The Three Contextual Gradients That Survive the 87-Test FDR Family",
         subtitle = paste(strwrap(
           "Group-specific slopes are from the diagnostic country-year fixed-effects bridge and are not numerically interchangeable with CRE coefficients. Only 3 of 87 pre-specified predictor-by-context omnibus tests survive BH correction.",
           width = 130), collapse = "\n"),
         x = NULL, y = "Diagnostic within-country slope") +
    theme_thesis() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7.6, angle = 20, hjust = 1))
  # >>> THESIS Figure 14 -- HIGH confidence, all three surviving predictor x dimension pairs and their per-group estimates verified against docx text word-for-word <<<
  sv(f14, "F46_three_contextual_gradients.png", 11, 5)
  f14
}, error = function(e) { message("F14 (thesis Figure 14) skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

# ============================================================================
# FIGURE B
# CLEAN EVIDENCE-LOCATION MAP
# ============================================================================
# Replacement candidate for the current evidence map.
#
# No z-scores, no metric soup.
# Each cell answers only:
#   Is the association established here?
#   How strong is the evidential grade?
#   What is the adjusted coefficient?
# ============================================================================

MAP_W <- EM[, .(
  code,
  label,
  domain,
  level = "Within-country change",
  grade = within_grade,
  estimate = estimate_within,
  counterdirection = counterdirection_within
)]

MAP_B <- EM[, .(
  code,
  label,
  domain,
  level = "Between-country differences",
  grade = between_grade,
  estimate = estimate_between,
  counterdirection = counterdirection_between
)]

MAP <- rbind(MAP_W, MAP_B, fill = TRUE)

MAP[, grade_score := fcase(
  grade == "Strong", 2L,
  grade == "Moderate", 1L,
  default = 0L
)]

# Order predictors:
# both-level evidence first, then strongest within/between signal.
ORDER_MAP <- MAP[, .(
  max_grade = max(grade_score, na.rm = TRUE),
  total_grade = sum(grade_score, na.rm = TRUE),
  max_beta = max(abs(estimate), na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(code, label, domain)]

ORDER_MAP[!is.finite(max_beta), max_beta := 0]

setorder(
  ORDER_MAP,
  -total_grade,
  -max_grade,
  -max_beta,
  domain,
  label
)

MAP[, label := factor(
  label,
  levels = rev(ORDER_MAP$label)
)]

MAP[, level := factor(
  level,
  levels = c(
    "Within-country change",
    "Between-country differences"
  )
)]

MAP[, cell_label := fifelse(
  grade == "Not established" | is.na(estimate),
  "—",
  sprintf("%.2f", estimate)
)]

MAP[, grade := factor(
  grade,
  levels = c(
    "Not established",
    "Moderate",
    "Strong"
  )
)]

GRADE_COL <- c(
  "Not established" = PAL$ground,
  "Moderate" = PAL$between,
  "Strong" = PAL$ink
)


f_map_clean <- ggplot(
  MAP,
  aes(x = level, y = label, fill = grade)
) +
  geom_tile(
    colour = PAL$rule,
    linewidth = .45
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = cell_label,
      colour = grade
    ),
    size = 2.75,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = GRADE_COL,
    name = "Evidence grade"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Not established" = PAL$muted,
      "Moderate" = PAL$ground,
      "Strong" = PAL$ground
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The evidence map: where is each association established?",
    subtitle =
      paste0(
        "Each column is a different estimand. Numbers are adjusted coefficients ",
        "in Cantril ladder points;\n",
        "a dash indicates that the association is not established after the ",
        "pre-specified evidential criteria."
      ),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption =
      paste0(
        "Strong = association survives multiplicity control and the designated ",
        "robustness/predictive criteria. Moderate = statistically established ",
        "but does not clear every robustness criterion. ",
        "The map locates evidence; it does not identify causal effects."
      )
  ) +
  theme_thesis(base = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 9.5
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 7.8
    ),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

  # >>> THESIS Figure 7 ("The Final Evidence Map Across All 29 National Predictors") -- HIGH confidence. This is the FINAL version; F01 earlier in the file is the superseded draft. <<<
sv(

  h = 11.5
)
